Computer.q: The word computer has been derived from which of the following language?
Computer.e: The word 'computer' is derived from the Latin word 'computare', which means to calculate, sum up, or reckon.

Computer.q: Input, output and processing devices grouped together represent a(n)
Computer.e: A computer system is a complete setup of integrated hardware components, including input devices, a processing unit (CPU), and output devices, working together.

Computer.q: Collecting the data and converting it into information is called
Computer.e: Processing is the step where raw data is converted into meaningful information.

Computer.q: Benefits of computers are
opts: very fast and can store huge amount of data
provide accurate output either input is correct or not
Computer.e: Computers are valued for their speed and large storage capacity. Accuracy depends on input.

Computer.q: A collection of unprocessed items is
Computer.e: Data refers to raw facts and figures before they are processed into information.

Computer.q: ______ is data that has been organised and presented in a meaningful fashion.
Computer.e: When data is processed into an understandable form, it becomes information.

Computer.q: The earliest calculating device is
Computer.e: The abacus, invented around 2400 BC, is the earliest known calculating device.

Computer.q: PCs are considered fourth-generation and contain
Computer.e: Fourth-generation computers introduced microprocessors in the 1970s.

Computer.q: Artificial Intelligence is an example of
Computer.e: Fifth-generation computers focus on AI and advanced computing.

Computer.q: Who developed integrated chip?
Computer.e: Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments invented the integrated circuit in 1958.

Computer.q: Computers that are portable and convenient to use for users who travel, are known as
Computer.e: Laptops are portable personal computers designed for mobility.

Computer.q: Desktop and personal computers are also known as
Computer.e: Personal computers are microcomputers designed for individual use.

Computer.q: This component is required to process data into information and consists of integrated circuits.
Computer.e: The CPU processes data into meaningful information using integrated circuits.

Computer.q: Where does computer add and compare data?
Computer.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs mathematical and logical operations.

Computer.q: CPU is fabricated as a single integrated circuit which is known as
Computer.e: A microprocessor is a CPU built on a single chip.

Computer.q: The main job of a CPU is to
Computer.e: The CPU processes data and executes instructions.

Computer.q: The CPU is made up of two smaller components
Computer.e: The CPU is composed of the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and CU (Control Unit).

Computer.q: The CPU comprises of control, memory and _____ units.
Computer.e: CPU includes Control Unit, Memory Unit, and Arithmetic/Logic Unit.

Computer.q: Computer is a/an
Computer.e: A computer is an electronic machine that processes information.

Computer.q: The father of computer is
Computer.e: Charles Babbage is considered the father of the computer for designing the Analytical Engine.

Computer.q: Analytical engine developed by
Computer.e: Charles Babbage developed the concept of the Analytical Engine in the 1830s.

Computer.q: Pascaline is also known by
Computer.e: Blaise Pascal invented the Pascaline, an early mechanical adding machine.

Computer.q: Who is the father of modern computer?
Computer.e: Alan Turing is considered the father of modern computing for his theoretical models.

Computer.q: 'Brain' of the computer is known as
Computer.e: The CPU is called the brain because it controls and processes all operations.

Computer.q: The _____ is responsible for performing calculations and contains decision making mechanisms.
Computer.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs calculations and logical decisions in the CPU.

Computer.q: Why RAM is so called?
opts: Because it is read and write memory
Because it is a volatile memory
Because it can be selected directly for storing and retrieving data and instructions of any location of chip
Because it is a non-volatile memory
Computer.e: RAM (Random Access Memory) allows data to be accessed randomly from any location.

Computer.q: Information stored in RAM need to be
Computer.e: RAM is volatile, so it requires refreshing to retain data while powered.

Computer.q: Storage that retains its data after the power is turned OFF is referred to as
Computer.e: Non-volatile storage like ROM or hard drives keeps data even without power.

Computer.q: What is called the permanent memory built into your computer?
Computer.e: ROM (Read Only Memory) stores permanent instructions like BIOS.

Computer.q: Permanent instructions that the computer use when it is turned ON and that cannot be changed by other instructions are contained in
Computer.e: ROM stores startup instructions and cannot be modified during normal use.

Computer.q: Which of the following is not a ROM?
Computer.e: EDPROM doesn’t exist; PROM, EPROM, and EEPROM are all ROM types.

Computer.q: When you first turn on a computer, instructions stored in the ______ the CPU is preset to execute
Computer.e: The BIOS stored in ROM is executed first when powering on a computer.

Computer.q: A disc's content that is recorded at the time of manufacture and that cannot be changed or erased by the user is
Computer.e: CD-ROM (Read-Only Memory) discs are pre-recorded and cannot be altered by users.

Computer.q: Which of the following computer's memory is characterised by low cost per bit stored?
Computer.e: Secondary storage like hard drives is cheaper per bit compared to primary storage (RAM).

Computer.q: Secondary storage
opts: consists of four main types of devices
does not store information for later retrieval
Computer.e: Secondary storage like hard disks keeps data even when power is off.

Computer.q: Which of the following is not used as secondary storage?
Computer.e: Semiconductor memory (RAM/ROM) is primary memory, not secondary storage.

Computer.q: The secondary storage devices can only store data but they cannot perform
Computer.e: Only the CPU performs arithmetic/logic operations; storage just stores data.

Computer.q: Where do you save the data, your data will remain intact even when the computer is turned OFF?
Computer.e: Data saved in secondary storage (hard disk, SSD) stays even when power is off.

Computer.q: Which of the following is the magnetic storage device?
Computer.e: Hard disks use magnetic coating to store data, unlike CDs which are optical.

Computer.q: The concentric circles on the floppy disk are further divided into
Computer.e: Floppy disks are divided into tracks and further into sectors for data storage.

Computer.q: The primary device that a computer uses to store information is
Computer.e: Hard drives are the main storage devices in computers for long-term data.

Computer.q: Hard disk devices are considered ______ storage.
Computer.e: Hard disks are non-volatile, retaining data without power.

Computer.q: Hard drive is used to store
Computer.e: Hard drives store permanent data until manually deleted.

Computer.q: Which is not an external storage device?
Computer.e: RAM is internal memory; CD, DVD, and Pen Drives are external storage.

Computer.q: Which of the following stores data permanently in a computer?
Computer.e: ROM permanently stores data like firmware.

Computer.q: Which of the following is an impact printer?
Computer.e: Daisy wheel printers physically strike the paper, making them impact printers.

Computer.q: The term 'gigabyte' refers to
Computer.e: 1 gigabyte = 1024 megabytes (in binary system).

Computer.q: A nibble is equal to ______ bits.
Computer.e: A nibble is 4 bits, half of a byte (8 bits).

Computer.q: Viruses, trojan horses and worms are
opts: unable to detect if present on computer
Computer.e: Viruses, worms, and trojans are malicious software that damage systems.

Computer.q: It is an act of intruding into someone else's computer or network
Computer.e: Hacking means unauthorized access to systems or networks.

Computer.q: A program designed to destroy data on your computer which can travel to 'infect' other computers is called a
Computer.e: A computer virus can corrupt data and spread between systems.

Computer.q: If your computer rebooting itself then it is likely that
opts: it does not have enough memory
there has been a power surge
Computer.e: Frequent unexpected reboots are common signs of malware or virus.

Computer.q: Computer virus is
Computer.e: A virus is a malicious software program.

Computer.q: The first PC virus was developed in
Computer.e: The first IBM PC virus, Brain, appeared in 1986.

Computer.q: The first computer virus is
Computer.e: The Creeper virus (1970s) is considered the first computer virus.

Computer.q: Which virus spreads in application software?
Computer.e: Macro viruses spread via application files like Word or Excel documents.

Computer.q: The ______ of a threat measures its potential impact on a system.
Computer.e: The degree of harm measures how much damage a threat can cause.

Computer.q: Which of the following is the type of software that has self-replicating software that causes damage to files and system?
Computer.e: Worms are self-replicating malware that spread across networks.

Computer.q: Like a virus, it is also a self-replicating program. The difference is it does not create copies of itself on one system; it propagates through networks. What does it refer here?
Computer.e: Worms spread over networks without attaching to host programs.

Computer.q: A worm
opts: can only be transferred with human intervention
Computer.e: Worms spread themselves across networks automatically.

Computer.q: Worm is a program that infects computer and spreads by inserting copies of itself into other executable code or documents.
Computer.e: Worms are self-replicating malware.

Computer.q: A computer virus normally attaches itself to another computer program known as a
Computer.e: A virus requires a host program to run and spread.

Computer.q: Viruses that fool a user into downloading and/or executing them by pretending to be useful applications are also sometimes called
Computer.e: Trojan horses disguise as legitimate programs.

Computer.q: A _____ is a small program embedded inside of a GIF image.
Computer.e: Spyware can be hidden in images like GIFs.

Computer.q: Hackers often gain entry to a network by pretending to be at a legitimate computer
Computer.e: IP spoofing disguises a malicious system as a trusted one.

Computer.q: Junk E-mail is also called
Computer.e: Unwanted bulk e-mail is known as spam.

Computer.q: Which of the following is used to prevent and detect malwares?
Computer.e: Antivirus software detects and removes malware.

Computer.q: A digital signature is
Computer.e: A digital signature is created by encrypting information for authentication.

Computer.q: A firewall operated by
opts: screening packets to / from the network and provide controllable filtering of network traffic
Computer.e: Firewalls screen and filter network traffic.

Computer.q: Passwords enable users to
Computer.e: Passwords secure data by maintaining confidentiality.

Computer.q: The programs designed to govern the computer hardware system are called the
Computer.e: System software (like operating systems) manages hardware resources.

Computer.q: A collection of various programs that helps control your computer is called
Computer.e: System software includes operating systems and utilities that manage computer resources.

Computer.q: A(n) ...... is a software that helps a computer control to operate efficiently and keep track of data.
Computer.e: Operating systems manage hardware and software resources for efficiency.

Computer.q: A computer cannot 'boot' if it does not have the
Computer.e: Without an operating system, the computer cannot start or manage resources.

Computer.q: Operating system is a
Computer.e: The OS is classified as system software because it manages hardware/software interaction.

Computer.q: ...... includes boot firmware and power management.
Computer.e: BIOS handles booting and power management during startup.

Computer.q: Which of the following is a system software?
Computer.e: Device drivers are system software that allow OS to communicate with hardware.

Computer.q: ...... helps in converting programming language to machine language.
Computer.e: Language translators (compilers, interpreters, assemblers) convert high-level code into machine code.

Computer.q: Grouping and processing all of a firm's transactions at one time is called
Computer.e: Batch processing collects data and processes it in groups instead of instantly.

Computer.q: Windows operating system is......
Computer.e: Windows is primarily a single-user system but supports multitasking.

Computer.q: Operating system that allows only one user to work on a computer at a time is known as
Computer.e: Single-user OS supports only one user at a time, e.g., MS-DOS.

Computer.q: ...... provides process and memory management services that allow two or more tasks, jobs, or programs to run simultaneously.
Computer.e: Multitasking OS allows multiple processes to run concurrently by sharing CPU time.

Computer.q: Which of the following terms explains the execution of more than one file at the same time on a single processor?
Computer.e: Multitasking allows running multiple programs on a single CPU.

Computer.q: ...... is a feature for scheduling and multi-programming to provide an economical interactive system of two or more users.
Computer.e: Time-sharing OS divides CPU time among users for interactive computing.

Computer.q: The simultaneous processing of two or more programs by multiple processors is
Computer.e: Multiprocessing uses multiple CPUs to execute multiple tasks simultaneously.

Computer.q: RTOS stands for
Computer.e: RTOS is designed for real-time applications where response time is critical.

Computer.q: System running more than one process concurrently are called
Computer.e: Multiprogramming lets multiple programs reside in memory and share CPU.

Computer.q: Which of the following refers to the means by which an OS or any other program interacts with the user?
Computer.e: A user interface (UI) enables communication between user and OS.

Computer.q: The first graphical user interface was designed by
Computer.e: Xerox Corporation (at PARC) developed the first GUI in the 1970s.

Computer.q: Application software
opts: is used to control the operating system
performs specific task for computer users
is used for making design only
Computer.e: Application software (Word, Excel) helps users perform specific tasks.

Computer.q: It shares characteristics with both hardware and software.
Computer.e: OS interacts directly with hardware (low level) and software (high level).

Computer.q: Which one of the following is not the function of operating system?
Computer.e: Networking is not a primary OS function, though modern OS support it.

Computer.q: Unix operating system is generally known as
Computer.e: Unix is a multi-user, multitasking operating system widely used in servers.

Computer.q: Which of the following operating systems is also known as single user operating system?
Computer.e: Classic MS-DOS is a single-user, single-tasking operating system.

Computer.q: A(n) device is any device that provides information, which is sent to the CPU.
Computer.e: Input devices like keyboard, mouse, and scanner send information to the CPU.

Computer.q: Information that comes from external source and fed into computer software is called
Computer.e: Data entered into the computer from outside sources is considered input.

Computer.q: This unit sends the processed results to the user.
Computer.e: The output unit delivers processed data to users through monitors, printers, etc.

Computer.q: Output unit includes
Computer.e: Output devices include printers, monitors, and plotters.

Computer.q: To move to the beginning of a line of text, press the key.
Computer.e: The "Home" key moves the cursor to the beginning of a line.

Computer.q: Shift, Ctrl, Alt are examples of which among the following category?
Computer.e: Modifier keys modify the function of other keys when pressed together.

Computer.q: Pointing device includes the following except
Computer.e: A keyboard is not a pointing device, unlike mouse, joystick, or trackball.

Computer.q: What type of device is a computer mouse?
Computer.e: A mouse is an input device that controls cursor movement.

Computer.q: First computer mouse was built by
Computer.e: Douglas Engelbart invented the first mouse in 1964.

Computer.q: Keyboard and ______ are the examples of input device.
Computer.e: Keyboards and mice are the most common input devices.

Computer.q: Trackball is an example of a/an
Computer.e: A trackball is a pointing device where a ball controls cursor movement.

Computer.q: A joystick is primarily used to/for
Computer.e: Joysticks are mainly used for gaming to control on-screen objects.

Computer.q: A device, which is used for making drawings, graphics and for menu selection
Computer.e: A light pen is a pointing device used for drawing directly on a screen.

Computer.q: ______ is generally used in applications like ATM, hospitals, airline reservation etc.
Computer.e: Touch screens allow direct interaction and are widely used in ATMs and kiosks.

Computer.q: The pattern of printed lines on most products are called
Computer.e: Barcodes are printed lines scanned for product identification.

Computer.q: Using output device one can
Computer.e: Output devices provide results to users, such as viewing on screen or printing.

Computer.q: What type of device is a computer monitor?
Computer.e: Monitors display processed data, making them output devices.

Computer.q: The higher the resolution of a monitor, the
Computer.e: Higher resolution means more pixels are packed closer, giving clearer images.

Computer.q: The most familiar output device for the micro computers is
Computer.e: The monitor is the most common output device for microcomputers.

Computer.q: The CRT is ______ in shape.
Computer.e: CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) screens are rectangular in shape.

Computer.q: ______ provides hard copy output on paper.
Computer.e: Printers provide physical (hard copy) output on paper.

Computer.q: ______ printer cannot print more than one character at a time.
Computer.e: Dot matrix printers print character by character using pins.

Computer.q: Speed of line printer is limited by the speed of
Computer.e: Line printer speed mainly depends on how fast paper can move.

Computer.q: An example of peripheral equipment is
Computer.e: Peripheral equipment refers to external devices like printers, not core CPU.

Computer.q: Which of the following group consists of only input devices?
Computer.e: Input devices include mouse, keyboard, and scanner. Monitor and printer are output.

Computer.q: Which of the following is a type of output device which produces the result in soft copy?
Computer.e: Monitors display results on screen (soft copy), unlike printers that give hard copies.

Computer.q: In MS-Word, Spelling Check is a feature available in which tab?
Computer.e: Proofing tools like Spelling & Grammar are on the Review tab.

Computer.q: When computer users ______ a document, they change its appearance.
Computer.e: According to the key, changing content/appearance is considered editing.

Computer.q: Which of the following is not an option of Edit menu?
Computer.e: Page Setup belongs to layout/print settings, not Edit.

Computer.q: Which bar is usually located below title bar that provides categorised options?
Computer.e: The menu bar lists grouped commands (File, Edit, View, etc.).

Computer.q: The process of making changes to an existing document is referred to as it.
Computer.e: Altering an existing document is editing.

Computer.q: To move to the beginning of a line of text, press the ... key.
Computer.e: Home moves the cursor to the start of the current line.

Computer.q: Which of the following is not a font style?

Computer.q: Portrait and landscape are
Computer.e: Portrait/landscape describe orientation of the page.

Computer.q: Which of the following should be used to move a paragraph from one place to another in a Word document?
Computer.e: Cut removes from original and Paste inserts at new location.

Computer.q: To move the text from its original position to another position without deleting it is called

Computer.q: For printing a document, you have to put on

Computer.q: What kind of software would you most likely use to keep track of a billing account?
Computer.e: Spreadsheets handle tabular data, calculations, and basic accounting.

Computer.q: A worksheet is made of columns and rows, wherein
opts: columns run horizontally and rows run vertically
columns run vertically and rows run horizontally
the run is dependent on the application being used
Computer.e: In spreadsheets, columns are vertical (A, B, C…) and rows are horizontal (1, 2, 3…).

Computer.q: Which software is most appropriate for numerical and statistical calculations?
Computer.e: Spreadsheets are built for numeric analysis and formulas.

Computer.q: Anything that is typed in a worksheet appears
opts: in both active cell and formula bar
Computer.e: Input shows in the active cell and the formula bar.

Computer.q: Which one is an example of spreadsheet package?
Computer.e: VisiCalc was an early spreadsheet program.

Computer.q: Which option will we use to give heading in the form?
Computer.e: Labels display fixed text like headings/captions.

Computer.q: The extension of a saved file in MS-Excel is

Computer.q: What does an electronic spreadsheet consist of?
Computer.e: Spreadsheets are made of rows, columns, and cells.

Computer.q: A collection of worksheets is called
Computer.e: Multiple worksheets together form a workbook.

Computer.q: All of the following terms are related to spreadsheet software except
Computer.e: Virus detection is a security function, not spreadsheet-specific.

Computer.q: Which of the following is an active cell in Excel?
Computer.e: The currently selected cell is the active/current cell.

Computer.q: Which of the following is a basic software of MS-Office?
Computer.e: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are core MS Office apps.

Computer.q: MS-Word is a
Computer.e: Word is designed for word processing.

Computer.q: Which software is used to create presentation?
Computer.e: PowerPoint creates slide presentations.

Computer.q: To open a new file in MS-Word, the shortcut key is
Computer.e: Ctrl+N creates a new document.

Computer.q: Which shortcut key is used to print the document?
Computer.e: Ctrl+P opens the Print dialog.

Computer.q: What is the default file extension of MS-Word document?
Computer.e: Older Word used .doc; newer versions default to .docx.

Computer.q: What do we call a network whose elements may be separated by some distance…?
Computer.e: Wide Area Networks span large geographic areas.

Computer.q: Ethernet, token ring and token bus are types of
Computer.e: They are LAN technologies/protocols.

Computer.q: The advantage of LAN is
Computer.e: LANs enable resource sharing like printers and storage.

Computer.q: Computer connected to a LAN can
opts: share information and/or share peripheral equipment
Computer.e: LANs allow users to share data and devices.

Computer.q: What is the use of bridge in network?
Computer.e: Bridges connect/segment LAN segments at the data link layer.

Computer.q: Which of the following refers to a small, single-site network?

Computer.q: These servers store and manage files for network users.
Computer.e: As per key: selected as Web server.

Computer.q: ______ is the most important/powerful computer in a typical network.

Computer.q: In HTML, tags consist of keywords enclosed within

Computer.q: Telnet is a

Computer.e: Telnet enables remote login and access.

Computer.q: What is the full form of VoIP?
Computer.e: VoIP means transmitting voice calls over IP networks.

Computer.q: The Internet service that provides a multimedia interface to available resources is called
Computer.e: The World Wide Web integrates text, images, audio, and video.

Computer.q: WWW stands for

Computer.q: What is a Website?
opts: A place from where we can get information in documents and files
A site that is owned by any particular company
A location on the world wide web
A place from where we can access Internet

Computer.q: A Website address is a unique name that identifies a specific ______ on the Web.
Computer.e: The unique address corresponds to a website.

Computer.q: A reference to data that reader can directly follow by selecting or hovering is

software program to delete a folder

Computer.e: According to key, web servers host and serve web pages.

An acronym for unlimited resource for learning

Computer.q: The Internet allows to
opts: connect to servers all around the world

Computer.q: The home page of a website is

Computer.e: Email communication is most like writing and sending a letter.

English.e: A “Cosmopolitan” considers himself a citizen of the world.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Of unknown authorship
English.e: A work without known author is called “Anonymous”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A person who rules without consulting the opinion of others
English.e: A ruler with absolute power is called an “Autocrat”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. One who is well versed in the science of female ailments
English.e: A doctor specializing in women’s diseases is called a “Gynecologist”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. One who eats everything
English.e: An “Omnivorous” person/animal eats both plants and animals.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. An elderly unmarried woman
English.e: An elderly unmarried woman is called a “Spinster”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A man who wastes his money on luxury
English.e: A person spending wastefully on luxuries is “Extravagant”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. To induce to have sexual intercourse
English.e: To lure someone into sexual relations is “Seduce”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Incapable of being seen through
English.e: Something that light cannot pass through is called “Opaque”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. One who sacrifices his life for a cause
English.e: A person who dies for a cause is a “Martyr”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A person coming to a foreign land to settle
English.e: One who settles in another country is an “Immigrant”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Murder of a king
English.e: Killing a king is called “Regicide”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. An associate in an office or institution
English.e: A fellow worker in an office is called a “Colleague”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. An official numbering of the population
English.e: The official population count is called a “Census”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A name assumed by a writer or a false name
English.e: A false name used by an author is called a “Pseudonym”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. One who believes in fate
English.e: A person who believes everything is pre-decided by fate is a “Fatalist”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. List of headings of the business to be transacted at a meeting
English.e: A list of matters to be discussed at a meeting is an “Agenda”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A government run by a dictator
English.e: Government ruled by one person with absolute power is “Autocracy”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. An office or post with no work but high pay
English.e: A lucrative office requiring little or no work is a “Sinecure”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Person who believes that God is everything and everything is God
English.e: A “Pantheist” believes God and the universe are identical.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Relationship by blood or birth
English.e: Blood relationship is called “Consanguinity”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Walking in sleep
English.e: Sleepwalking is called “Somnambulism”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A person who kills somebody especially for political reason
English.e: A political killer is called an “Assassin”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Study of mankind
English.e: The scientific study of humans is “Anthropology”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. Through which light cannot pass
English.e: Material that blocks light is “Opaque”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A person not sure of the existence of God
English.e: A person uncertain about God’s existence is an “Agnostic”.

English.q: Choose the alternative which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. One who deserts his religion
English.e: A person who renounces or abandons his faith is called an “Apostate”.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). By this time next year he has had settled himself in London.
English.e: Use 'will have settled' instead of 'has had settled' because the sentence requires the future perfect tense.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Whenever you are coming here you bring a lot of sweets for me.
opts: a lot of sweets for me
English.e: Replace 'you are coming' with 'you come'. The present indefinite tense is used to express habitual actions.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The vehicle which is stopped by the policeman contained a number of smuggled watches.
English.e: Use 'was stopped' instead of 'is stopped' because the verb 'contained' shows the action is in the past.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). I could not recall what he has told me about her concern with Mahesh.
English.e: Use 'had told' instead of 'has told'. Since the reporting verb is in the past, the subordinate clause should also be in the past perfect.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He told me that he wrote a letter to his superior for a certain reason.
opts: to his superior for a certain reason
English.e: Use 'had written' instead of 'wrote'. The past perfect tense is needed for an action completed before another past action.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Once he realises that he commits a mistake he admits and corrects it without delay.
opts: he admits and corrects it without delay
English.e: Use 'has committed' instead of 'commits'. The context requires the present perfect to indicate a completed action.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). I knew our college library was run chaotically but only recently did I discover how bad the situation is.
opts: I knew our college library was run chaotically
but only recently did I discover
English.e: Replace 'is' with 'was'. The whole sentence is in the past tense, so the verb must agree.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). When it comes to comparison between the two, quality is most important than quantity.
opts: When it comes to comparison between the two
English.e: Use 'more' instead of 'most' because 'more' is used for comparison between two things, not 'most'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The two or three first chapters of most of the novels are dull reading.
opts: The two or three first chapters
English.e: It should be 'The first two or three chapters' because ordinals (first, second, etc.) are placed before cardinals (two, three, etc.).

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). In the opinion of everyone she is wiser than beautiful.
English.e: Use 'more wise' instead of 'wiser' because when comparing two qualities of the same person, we use 'more' with the positive degree, not the comparative form.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Some people get used to changes very easily than others do.
English.e: Replace 'very easily' with 'more easily' because a comparative degree is required before 'than'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). These problems are too smallest or localised for the government to handle efficiently.
English.e: Use 'small' instead of 'smallest'. Superlative degree is not used after 'too'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Geometry and drawing are more easier than geography and social studies.
English.e: Delete 'more'. 'Easier' itself is comparative, so a double comparative 'more easier' is incorrect.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He has a scheme of his own which he thinks preferable than that of any other person's.
opts: He has a scheme of his own
English.e: Replace 'preferable than' with 'preferable to'. The word 'prefer' and its forms always take 'to' for comparison.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He was very tired of work, so he said that he was sorry not to accompany us.
opts: He was very tired of work
so he said that he was
English.e: The sentence is correct. No error.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). We are confident enough to earn our livelihood by toiling hardly.
English.e: Use 'hard' instead of 'hardly'. 'Hard' means with great effort, while 'hardly' means 'almost not'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He walked quick so that he would not be late.
English.e: Replace 'quick' with 'quickly'. Verbs are modified by adverbs, so 'walked' requires 'quickly'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). You seem to be enough rich to buy anything you like.
English.e: It should be 'rich enough'. The word 'enough' is generally placed after adjectives, not before.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). She looked at him lovely but he did not respond to her.
English.e: Use 'lovingly' instead of 'lovely'. 'Lovely' is an adjective, while 'lovingly' is the adverb needed here.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). It had been too cold the whole month and we preferred staying in the plains.
opts: the whole month and we preferred
English.e: Use 'very' instead of 'too'. 'Too' suggests excess, while 'very' indicates a high degree, which is correct here.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). I refused to accompany him because I was so tired.
English.e: Replace 'so' with 'very'. 'Very' expresses a high degree, while 'so' requires a following clause (e.g., so...that).

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). It is only after the war is over that people realise how bad it was.
opts: It is only after the war
English.e: Use 'a' in place of 'the' because 'the war' indicates a non-specific war.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Children who have had good Pre-school Education are most likely to out do other children at school.
opts: good Pre-school Education are most likely
to out do other children at school
English.e: Use 'a' before 'good' because "good Pre-school Education" is a singular countable noun here.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). We should drink several glasses of the water daily if we want to remain healthy.
opts: if we want to remain healthy
English.e: Delete 'the' before 'water' because 'water' is uncountable. We cannot count water itself, only its measure.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). I am not wealthy, so I cannot afford to buy a expensive car.
English.e: Use 'an' instead of 'a' because 'expensive' begins with a vowel sound.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He was an atheist but now-a-days he goes to the church and offers prayers for hours.
opts: but now-a-days he goes to the church
English.e: Delete 'the' before 'church'. Articles are omitted before places like school, college, church, market when visited for their primary purpose.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). It was by the mistake that he caught her hand.
English.e: Delete 'the' because 'by mistake' is a fixed phrase.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). We have carefully considered the importance of issues raised in the report.
English.e: Remove 'the' because 'issues' is indefinite here. 'The' should only be used with definite, specific issues.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). As soon as he opened the old wooden box than a rat jumped out of it.
opts: the old wooden box than a rat
English.e: Remove 'than'. We say "As soon as...," not "As soon as...than."

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Though he ran fast still he could not escape from the police.
English.e: Replace 'still' with 'yet' (or use a comma). 'Though/Although' is followed by 'yet' in standard usage.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The robber had hardly put the ornaments in his bag than the housewife woke up.
opts: put the ornaments in his bag
English.e: Replace 'than' with 'when'. 'Hardly' is followed by 'when' or 'before,' not 'than.'

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Unless you do not take care of your health, you will continue to suffer.
English.e: Remove 'do not'. 'Unless' already gives a negative sense, so double negation is wrong.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). As they were in trouble therefore they did not attend the marriage.
English.e: Remove 'therefore'. 'As' and 'since' already provide the reason, so 'therefore' is redundant.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). This is not such a major problem which cannot be solved with a little effort.
opts: This is not such a major
English.e: Replace 'which' with 'that'. After 'such,' we use 'that' or 'as,' not 'which.'

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The guide told us that where the island was and went on narrating its history.
opts: and went on narrating its history
English.e: Remove 'that'. Interrogative words (where, when, who, etc.) are not preceded by 'that.'

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). I have not gone through the letter and so I am not aware of its content.
opts: I have not gone through the letter
English.e: Use 'contents' instead of 'content' because 'contents' (plural) refers to the things contained in something.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). What is the criteria of selection in the examination?
English.e: Use 'criterion' instead of 'criteria'. 'Criterion' is singular, while 'criteria' is plural. Since the question uses "What is," the singular form is required.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He uses a fine quality of shampoo so his hairs are black and attractive.
opts: so his hairs are black and attractive
English.e: Replace 'hairs are' with 'hair is'. The word 'hair' is generally uncountable and used in the singular form.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The table's wood is infested with mite and I am likely to dispose it off.
opts: with mite and I am likely
English.e: Use 'The wood of the table' instead of "The table's wood." Possessive case is usually used with living things, not non-living objects.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The issue are very complex and the problem is that they are bound to be obscured by these hypocritical politicians.
opts: and the problem is that they are bound to be
English.e: Use 'The issues' because the verb 'are' indicates the noun must be plural.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Alumnus of the college are invited to college functions every year.
English.e: Use 'Alumni' instead of 'Alumnus'. 'Alumnus' refers to one male student, while 'Alumni' is the plural, which matches the sentence meaning.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The hills of the Uttar Pradesh abound in beautiful sceneries and visitors are attracted to it every year.
opts: The hills of the Uttar Pradesh
and visitors are attracted to it every year
English.e: Replace 'sceneries' with 'scenery'. Words like 'scenery', 'furniture', 'poetry' are always used in the singular form.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). While she was returning from college, a ruffian attacked on her with a dagger.
opts: While she was returning from college
English.e: Remove 'on'. The verb 'attack' is transitive and directly takes an object, so 'attacked her' is correct.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). This book deals in the burning problems our country is facing at present.
English.e: Replace 'deals in' with 'deals with'. 'Deal in' means to trade, while 'deal with' means to handle or discuss a subject.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The elegantly designed collection for ladies has an emphasis with variety, style and colour.
English.e: Replace 'with' with 'on'. We say "emphasis on something," not "emphasis with."

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Despite of a good monsoon this year, the production of food grains in the country did not go up.
opts: Despite of a good monsoon this year
in the country did not go up
English.e: Remove 'of'. We say "despite something," not "despite of."

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The accused was bound by a chain and taken to prison.
English.e: Use 'bound with a chain' instead of 'bound by a chain'. 'With' is used to indicate the instrument.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). His father is sick but he does not look for him.
English.e: Use 'look after' instead of 'look for'. 'Look for' means search, while 'look after' means take care of.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). It was, in fact, her father who prevented her at joining the police academy.
English.e: Replace 'at' with 'from'. We say "prevent someone from doing something."

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The teacher was busy and asked three of we to divide the work and do it.
opts: to divide the work and do it
English.e: Use 'us' instead of 'we' because a pronoun after a preposition should be in the objective case.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). One should always remember that it is his duty to help the weak and the poor.
opts: to help the weak and the poor
English.e: Use 'one’s duty' instead of 'his duty' because the subject 'one' is an indefinite pronoun, and the pronoun must agree.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). This is the best which we can do in the present circumstances.
English.e: Replace 'which' with 'that'. 'That' is used in defining clauses, while 'which' is used in both defining and non-defining clauses.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He is not one of these who will help everybody whom he meets.
opts: He is not one of these
English.e: It should be 'whom they meet' because the relative pronoun must agree in number and person with its antecedent ('these').

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The principal ordered the peon to let the boys and I go in.
opts: the boys and I go in
English.e: It should be 'the boys and me' because a pronoun after 'let' is in the objective case.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). She is a woman who I know you can always rely upon.
English.e: Replace 'who' with 'whom' because 'whom' is used in the objective case when not followed directly by a verb.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He and myself alone will complete this work because we don't need the help of anyone.
opts: we don't need the help of anyone
English.e: It should be 'He and I' instead of 'He and myself'. 'Myself' is a reflexive pronoun and should only be used when the subject and object are the same.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Sunil would had got this offer if he had attended the interview.
English.e: Use 'would have' instead of 'would had' because 'have' is used after modal auxiliaries.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Did I not informed you about the details of our visit to different work stations?
English.e: Use 'inform' instead of 'informed' because the helping verb 'did' is already in the past tense.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The children were playing with a ball and run around when the accident occurred.
opts: run around when the accident occurred
English.e: Replace 'run around' with 'running around' to maintain verb form consistency with 'were playing'.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). Hardly had he threw the ball when it fell on the ground.
English.e: Use 'thrown' instead of 'threw'. After 'had', the past participle form of the verb is required.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He dared to go at the blast site so as to save his colleague.
English.e: The sentence is correct. No error.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He feels that I cannot imagine what a space station would be looked like.
English.e: Replace 'would be looked like' with 'would look like' because 'look' functions as a linking verb here.

English.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose option (D). They asked the guide whether they could wait and watched the pictures after sunset.
English.e: Use 'watch' instead of 'watched' because it follows 'could', which takes the base form of the verb.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: Mohan said, "I want to visit my friends this weekend".
opts: Mohan said he wants to visit his friends that weekend.
Mohan said he wanted to visit his friends that weekend.
Mohan said he wanted to visit his friends this weekend.
Mohan said he wants to visit his friends this weekend.
English.e: Direct → Indirect: Present simple/want → Past simple/wanted. "This weekend" → "that weekend".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: They said, "We've lived here for a long time."
opts: They said they have lived there for a long time.
They said they lived here for a long time.
They said they had lived there for a long time.
They said they had lived there for a long time.
English.e: Present perfect ("have lived") → Past perfect ("had lived"). "Here" → "there".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He asked me, "Have you finished reading the newspaper?"
opts: He asked me if had I finished reading the newspaper.
He asked me if I had finished reading the newspaper.
He asked me if I would finish reading the newspaper.
He asked me if I would be finishing reading the newspaper.
English.e: Question in present perfect → Past perfect in indirect. Interrogatives use "if/whether".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "I get up every morning at seven o'clock", Peter said.
opts: Peter said he got up every morning at seven o'clock.
Peter said I got up every morning at seven o'clock.
Peter said he had got up every morning at seven o'clock.
Peter said he gets up every morning at seven o'clock.
English.e: Habitual actions (present simple truths) usually remain unchanged in indirect speech.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I came here yesterday".
opts: He said that he went there the previous day.
He said that he had come there the previous day.
He said that he came there yesterday.
He inquired that he had come there the previous day.
English.e: Past simple → Past perfect. "Yesterday" → "the previous day".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "I never eat fish," he explained.
opts: He explained that he never ate fish.
He explained that he never eats fish.
He explained that he has never eaten fish.
English.e: Present simple ("eat") → Past simple ("ate"). Reporting verb in past changes tense.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "I have bought a house," he said.
opts: He said that he had bought a house.
He said that he has bought a house.
He said that he bought a house.
He said that he would buy a house.
English.e: Present perfect → Past perfect in indirect speech.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "Wish you a happy journey," Neeta said to me.
opts: Neeta told me that I should wish a happy journey.
Neeta wished me a happy journey.
Neeta told me to have a happy journey.
Neeta wished me that I wish a happy journey.
English.e: Expressions of wishing are changed to "wished" in indirect speech.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: You say, "I cut the finger".
opts: You say that you cut the finger.
You said that you had cut the finger.
You say that I cut the finger.
You said that I had cut the finger.
English.e: Reporting verb "say" in present → no change in tense.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "I know this area because I used to live here," he informed.
opts: He informed that he knew that area because he used to live there.
He informed that he knew that area because he had lived there.
He informed that he knew that area because he had been living there.
He informed that he knew that area because he lived there.
English.e: "Know" → "knew"; "here" → "there"; "used to" remains unchanged.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "How smart you are!" she said.
opts: She exclaimed that I am smart.
She exclaimed that he was very smart.
She exclaimed that she is smart.
English.e: Exclamations → "She exclaimed that…". Present → Past.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: The kidnappers said, "If you do not pay the ransom, we'll kill the boy."
opts: The kidnappers threatened to kill the boy if they did not pay the ransom.
The kidnappers said that if they paid not the ransom, they will kill the boy.
The kidnappers said to them that if you do not pay the ransom, we shall kill the boy.
The kidnappers threatened that if the parents of the boy did not pay the ransom the boy will be killed.
English.e: Threats in indirect → "threatened to…". Future (will) → Conditional (would).

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "Ugh! There's a slug in my lettuce. Waiter!" he cried.
opts: He said ugh that there was a slug in his lettuce and asked the waiter to come.
He exclaimed with disgust that there was a slug in his lettuce and called the waiter.
He said to the waiter that ugh there was a slug in his lettuce.
He asked the waiter that there was a slug in his lettuce.
English.e: Exclamations with disgust → "He exclaimed with disgust…". Imperative → "called the waiter".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "You used to be good at Grammar," said I. "Why have you neglected it?"
opts: I said that he used to be good at Grammar and said why he had neglected it.
I said to him that he had been good at grammar and wanted to know why he had neglected it.
I reminded him that he used to be good at grammar and asked why he had neglected it.
I asked him that why had he neglected grammar when he used to be good at it.
English.e: Past habit ("used to") remains same. Present perfect ("have neglected") → Past perfect ("had neglected").

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: I invited Rama to come for a drive the following day.
opts: I said to Rama, "Will you come for a drive the following day?"
I said to Rama, "Will you come for a drive the next day?"
I put a question to Rama, "Will you come for a drive the day following?"
I said, "Rama, would you like to come for a drive tomorrow?"
English.e: "The following day" in indirect → "tomorrow" in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I want to talk to you."
opts: He said he wanted to talk to you.
He said that he wanted to talk to him.
He says that he wanted to talk to you.
He had said that he wanted to talk with him.
English.e: Present simple ("want") → Past simple ("wanted"). Pronoun change: "you" → "him/her".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: "I am going to Delhi," he declared.
opts: He said that he was going to Delhi.
He was going to Delhi he declared.
He declared that he was going to Delhi.
He declares that he is going to Delhi.
English.e: Present continuous ("am going") → Past continuous ("was going").

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: Ram said, "Good morning, Sir."
opts: Ram wished a good morning to Sir.
Ram declared it was a good morning.
Ram wished his sir a good morning.
English.e: Greetings → "wished…".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: Esha said, "Please lend me the book, Asha."
opts: Esha requested Asha to lend her the book.
Esha said that the book be lent to her.
Esha demanded from Asha the book.
English.e: "Please + verb" → request. Imperative in indirect = "requested + object + to + V1".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "Two and three is five."
opts: He said that two and three are five.
He said that two and three is five.
He said that two and three was five.
He said that two and three were five.
English.e: Universal truths or facts → No tense change.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that he had lost his wallet.
opts: He said, "I had lost my wallet."
He said, "I have lost my wallet."
English.e: Past perfect in indirect remains past perfect in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: John said, "I can solve this problem."
opts: John said he could solve that problem.
John said he can solve that problem.
John said he was able to solve this problem.
John said he will solve that problem.
English.e: "Can" → "could" in indirect. "This" → "that".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She told me that she would call me the next day.
opts: She said, "I will call you tomorrow."
She said, "I would call you tomorrow."
She said, "I will call you the next day."
She said, "I shall call you the following day."
English.e: "Would" in indirect → "will" in direct. "Next day" → "tomorrow".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I may join the party tonight."
opts: He said that he might join the party that night.
He said that he may join the party tonight.
He said he could join the party that night.
He said that he might be joining the party tonight.
English.e: "May" → "might". "Tonight" → "that night".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: The teacher told the students that honesty is the best policy.
opts: The teacher said to the students, "Honesty is the best policy."
The teacher said to the students, "Honesty was the best policy."
The teacher told the students, "Honesty had been the best policy."
The teacher said to the students, "Honesty will be the best policy."
English.e: Universal truths (is the best policy) → no tense change.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I was working on a project."
opts: He said that he had been working on a project.
He said that he was working on a project.
He said he had worked on a project.
He said he works on a project.
English.e: Past continuous → Past perfect continuous.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She said that she could swim across the river.
opts: She said, "I could swim across the river."
She said, "I can swim across the river."
She said, "I was able to swim across the river."
She said, "I may swim across the river."
English.e: "Could" in indirect (reporting past) → "can" in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: The boy said, "I have been waiting for two hours."
opts: The boy said he was waiting for two hours.
The boy said he had been waiting for two hours.
The boy said he has been waiting for two hours.
The boy said that he waited for two hours.
English.e: Present perfect continuous → Past perfect continuous.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that he had been studying all night.
opts: He said, "I have studied all night."
He said, "I had been studying all night."
He said, "I have been studying all night."
English.e: Past perfect continuous remains the same in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I will help you if I can."
opts: She said that she will help me if she can.
She said she would help me if she could.
She said that she can help me if she may.
She said she should help me if she could.
English.e: "Will" → "would"; "can" → "could".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He told me that he had been playing football since morning.
opts: He said, "I am playing football since morning."
He said, "I have been playing football since morning."
He said, "I had been playing football since morning."
He said, "I was playing football since morning."
English.e: Past perfect continuous in indirect remains the same in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I don’t like tea."
opts: She said that she doesn’t like tea.
She said that she didn’t like tea.
She said that she hadn’t liked tea.
She said she won’t like tea.
English.e: Present simple → Past simple.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that the Earth moves around the Sun.
opts: He said, "The Earth moved around the Sun."
He said, "The Earth moves around the Sun."
He said, "The Earth has moved around the Sun."
He said, "The Earth is moving around the Sun."
English.e: Scientific facts → No tense change in reported speech.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She asked, "Where do you live?"
opts: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I had lived.
She asked me where was I living.
English.e: Interrogative present simple → Past simple in indirect.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He asked me where I was going.
opts: He asked me, "Where you are going?"
He asked me, "Where are you going?"
He asked me, "Where I was going?"
He asked me, "Where was I going?"
English.e: Indirect question → Direct question uses normal question form.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I will be travelling tomorrow."
opts: She said she would be travelling the next day.
She said she will be travelling tomorrow.
She said she is travelling the next day.
She said she was travelling tomorrow.
English.e: Future continuous → "would be + V-ing". "Tomorrow" → "the next day".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that he had written a letter.
opts: He said, "I have written a letter."
He said, "I had written a letter."
English.e: Past perfect in indirect remains the same in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "Do you know the answer?"
opts: She asked me if I had known the answer.
She asked me if I know the answer.
She asked me if I knew the answer.
She asked me if I was knowing the answer.
English.e: Interrogative → "asked if/whether". Present → Past.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She asked me if I liked coffee.
English.e: Indirect yes/no question → Direct with "do/does".

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "Let us go for a walk."
opts: He suggested that they should go for a walk.
He said that they must go for a walk.
He said that they had to go for a walk.
He ordered them to go for a walk.
English.e: "Let us" → Suggestion form in indirect speech.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He suggested that we should play football.
English.e: Suggestion in indirect → "Let’s…" in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said to me, "Please open the window."
opts: She requested me to open the window.
She told me to open the window.
She asked me open the window.
She demanded me to open the window.
English.e: Polite request → "requested + object + to + V1".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She requested me to lend her some money.
opts: She said, "Please lend me some money."
English.e: "Requested to" → "Please + V1" in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "Hurrah! We have won the match."
opts: He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
He exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
He said with joy that they win the match.
He exclaimed that they have won the match.
English.e: Exclamations with joy → "exclaimed with joy that…".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He exclaimed with sorrow that he had failed the exam.
opts: He said, "I will fail the exam."
He said, "Alas! I have failed the exam."
He said, "Alas! I failed the exam."
English.e: "Exclaimed with sorrow" → "Alas!" in direct speech.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I must finish this work today."
opts: He said that he had to finish that work that day.
He said that he must finish that work today.
He said that he should finish that work today.
He said that he must have finished that work that day.
English.e: "Must" → "had to" (obligation). "Today" → "that day".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that he had to complete the assignment.
opts: He said, "I must complete the assignment."
He said, "I have to complete the assignment."
He said, "I had to complete the assignment."
He said, "I should complete the assignment."

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I was cooking dinner when he arrived."
opts: She said she cooked dinner when he arrived.
She said that she had been cooking dinner when he arrived.
She said she was cooking dinner when he had arrived.
She said she had cooked dinner when he arrived.
English.e: Past continuous + simple past → Past perfect continuous + simple past.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She said that she had been cooking dinner when he arrived.
opts: She said, "I was cooking dinner when he arrived."
She said, "I cooked dinner when he arrived."
She said, "I had cooked dinner when he arrived."
She said, "I have been cooking dinner when he arrived."

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "I will have finished the work by 6 pm."

He said that he would have finished the work by 6 pm.
He said he will finish the work by 6 pm.
He said that he finished the work by 6 pm.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He said that he would have finished the work by 6 pm.
opts: He said, "I will finish the work by 6 pm."
He said, "I will have finished the work by 6 pm."
He said, "I finished the work by 6 pm."
He said, "I had finished the work by 6 pm."

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I cannot swim."
opts: She said that she could not swim.
She said that she couldn’t swim.

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She said that she could not swim.
English.e: "Could not" in indirect generally comes from "cannot" in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "Did you see the movie yesterday?"
opts: He asked me if I saw the movie yesterday.
He asked me if I had seen the movie the previous day.
He asked me did I see the movie the previous day.
He asked me whether I see the movie yesterday.
English.e: Past simple question → Past perfect in indirect. "Yesterday" → "the previous day".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: He asked me if I had seen the movie the previous day.
opts: He said, "Have you seen the movie yesterday?"
He asked, "Did you see the movie yesterday?"
He asked, "Do you see the movie yesterday?"
He asked, "Were you seeing the movie yesterday?"
English.e: Past perfect indirect → Past simple direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: She said, "I hope you will succeed."
opts: She said that she hoped I would succeed.
She said she hopes I will succeed.
She said she was hoping I would succeed.
She said she hoped that I succeed.
English.e: "Hope" → "hoped"; "will" → "would".

English.q: Change from Indirect to Direct speech: She said that she hoped I would succeed.
opts: She said, "I hope you will succeed."
She said, "I hoped you will succeed."
She said, "I hope you would succeed."
English.e: Past hope in indirect → Present hope in direct.

English.q: Change from Direct to Indirect speech: He said, "Let me help you with this work."
opts: He offered to help me with that work.
He asked if he might help me with this work.
He said that he helps me with the work.
He said he was helping me with the work.
English.e: "Let me + V1" → Offer in indirect speech.

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: The students are decorating the stage for the annual day celebrations.
opts: The stage had been decorated by the students for the annual day celebrations.
The stage is being decorated by the students for the annual day celebrations.
The stage was decorated by the students for the annual day celebrations.
The stage has been decorated by the students for the annual day celebrations.
English.e: Present Continuous tense (is/are + V-ing) changes to 'is/am/are + being + V3' in Passive voice. Since 'stage' is singular, we use 'is being decorated'.

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: Quinine tastes bitter.
opts: Quinine is bitter when it is tasted.
The taste of quinine is bitter.
English.e: Simple present tense active with “taste” → Passive = "is…when it is tasted." Option (A) keeps the meaning intact.

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: The vintage cars hold a special place in the hearts of their owners.
opts: A special place in the hearts of the vintage car owners is held by them.
A special place was held by the vintage cars in the hearts of their owners.
A special place is held by the vintage cars in the hearts of their owners.
A special place is being held by the vintage cars in the hearts of their owners.
English.e: Present simple (hold) → Passive = is/are held + object. Correct form is "is held."

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: He asked me to finish the work in time.
opts: I was asked that I should finish the work in time.
He asked me that I should finish the work in time.
I was asked to finish the work in time.
I was asked to finish the work in time by him.
English.e: “asked me to do” → Passive = “I was asked to do…” Compact form is (C).

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: What amused you?
opts: What you are made to amuse by?
By what are you being amused?
By what have you been amused?
English.e: Interrogative past tense → Passive = "By what + were + subject + V3."

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: Close the doors.
opts: The doors are to be closed.
English.e: Imperative sentences → Passive = "Let + object + be + V3."

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: None likes him.
opts: He was not liked by anyone.
He has not been liked by anyone.
He is not liked by anyone.
English.e: Present simple negative → Passive = is/are not + V3.

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: You are requested to keep the book on the table.
opts: You should keep the book on the table.
You must keep the book on the table.
Please kept the book on the table.
Please keep the book on the table.
English.e: Passive polite request ("you are requested") → Active = “Please + V1.”

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: People say that he is a spy.
opts: It was said that he is a spy.
It is said by people that he is a spy.
It has been said that he is a spy.
It is said that he is a spy.
English.e: "People say" → Passive impersonal = "It is said that…".

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: The task should have been completed by the student.
opts: The student should have completed the task.
The student should complete the task.
The student should be completing the task.
The student should have complete the task.
English.e: Modal perfect passive (should have been + V3) → Active = "should have + V3."

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: The child upset the salt over everything.
opts: The child is upset about the salt over everything.
The salt is upset over everything by the child.
The salt is upsetted by the child over everything.
The salt was upset over everything by the child.
English.e: Past simple active → Passive = was/were + V3. Correct = "was upset."

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: Please see that the room is swept and mopped before I return.
opts: Please see that somebody will sweeps and mop the room before I return.
Please see that somebody has swept and mopped the room before I return.
Please see that somebody sweeps and mops the room before I return.
Please see that somebody is sweeping and mops the room before I return.
English.e: Passive "is swept and mopped" → Active = "somebody sweeps and mops."

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: You are requested to offer your remarks.
opts: You have been requested to offer your remarks.
You were requested to offer your remarks.
You are being requested to offer your remarks.
English.e: Passive request structure → Active polite form = "Kindly offer…"

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: We prohibit smoking.
English.e: Present simple → Passive = "is/are + V3." Correct form = "Smoking is prohibited."

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: The manager will review the applications tomorrow.
opts: The applications are reviewed by the manager tomorrow.
The applications were reviewed by the manager tomorrow.
The applications will be reviewed by the manager tomorrow.
The applications have been reviewed by the manager tomorrow.

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: The match was won by our team.
opts: Our team has won the match.
Our team will win the match.
English.e: Past simple passive (was + V3) → Active = simple past.

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: They are building a new hospital near the park.
opts: A new hospital has been built near the park.
A new hospital was built near the park.
A new hospital is being built near the park.
A new hospital will be built near the park.

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: The decision has been taken by the committee.
opts: The committee has taken the decision.
The committee will take the decision.
English.e: Present perfect passive (has been + V3) → Active = has/have + V3.

This poem is written by whom?
This poem was written by whom?
By whom was this poem written?

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: The thief has been caught by the police.

The police will catch the thief.

English.q: Change from Active to Passive voice: They will announce the results next week.

The results will be announced next week.

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: The work is being completed by the students.

The plants have been watered by the gardener every morning.

English.q: Change from Passive to Active voice: Dinner is being prepared by my mother.
