GK.q: Who was the founder of the Maurya dynasty?
GK.e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 322 BCE by defeating the Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya). He established the first pan-Indian empire before abdicating in favor of his son, Bindusara.

GK.q: Who composed the Arthashastra, an important text on politics and administration?
GK.e: The Arthashastra was composed by Kautilya (Chanakya), the prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya. It discusses administration, diplomacy, taxation, law, war strategies, and economics in ancient India.

GK.q: The capital of Magadha under Bimbisara was
GK.e: Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty made Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir in Bihar) his capital. Later, Ajatashatru shifted the capital to Pataliputra.

GK.q: Which ruler is associated with the first Buddhist Council?
GK.e: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha in 483 BCE after the death of Buddha. It was patronized by Ajatashatru and presided over by Mahakassapa.

GK.q: Who was the last ruler of the Maurya dynasty?
GK.e: Brihadratha was the last Maurya ruler. He was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE, which led to the foundation of the Shunga dynasty.

GK.q: The term "Upanishad" literally means
GK.e: "Upanishad" means sitting near the guru to receive secret spiritual knowledge. They are philosophical texts that explain the essence of the Vedas and concepts like Brahman, Atman, and Moksha.

GK.q: Who was the contemporary of Alexander the Great in India?
GK.e: When Alexander invaded India in 326 BCE, the ruler of Magadha was Dhana Nanda of the Nanda dynasty. Chandragupta Maurya later overthrew him with the help of Chanakya.

GK.q: The famous "Nasik Inscription" is associated with which dynasty?
GK.e: The Nasik inscription, written by Gautami Balashri (mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni), describes the achievements of the Satavahana ruler Gautamiputra Satakarni.

GK.q: The Great Bath has been found at which Indus Valley Civilization site?
GK.e: The Great Bath is one of the most remarkable structures of Mohenjo-daro. It was likely used for ritual bathing and indicates the importance of water in religious practices of Harappan people.

GK.q: Who was the author of "Indica"?
GK.e: Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador in the court of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote "Indica." It gives valuable information about Mauryan administration, society, and culture.

GK.q: The Rigveda consists of how many hymns?
GK.e: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and contains 1028 hymns divided into 10 Mandalas. It reflects early Vedic religion and society.

GK.q: Who was the founder of the Gupta dynasty?
GK.e: Sri Gupta founded the Gupta dynasty around 240 CE. His successors, especially Chandragupta I and Samudragupta, expanded it into a powerful empire.

GK.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the "Napoleon of India"?
GK.e: Samudragupta is called the "Napoleon of India" (by V. A. Smith) due to his military conquests across India. The Prayag Prashasti describes his achievements.

GK.q: The famous "Iron Pillar" at Mehrauli, Delhi, was built by which ruler?
GK.e: The Iron Pillar was constructed during the Gupta period under Chandragupta II. It has not rusted for over 1600 years, showing advanced metallurgical skills.

GK.q: Which Buddhist council was held during the reign of Kanishka?
GK.e: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under the patronage of Kanishka (Kushan dynasty). It led to the division of Buddhism into Mahayana and Hinayana sects.

GK.q: The "Allahabad Pillar Inscription" is associated with which Gupta ruler?
GK.e: The Allahabad Pillar Inscription, composed by Harisena, describes Samudragupta’s conquests and is a key source for Gupta history.

GK.q: The "Harshacharita" was written by
GK.e: "Harshacharita" was written by Banabhatta in the 7th century CE. It describes the life and reign of King Harshavardhana.

GK.q: Which Harappan site is known for its dockyard?
GK.e: Lothal (in Gujarat) is famous for its dockyard, bead-making industry, and evidence of trade with Mesopotamia.

GK.q: The practice of Sati was first banned by which ruler?
GK.e: Harshavardhana (7th century CE) banned the inhuman practice of Sati in his empire. However, it reappeared in later centuries.

GK.q: Which Chinese traveler visited the court of Harshavardhana?
GK.e: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang), a Chinese Buddhist monk, visited India in the 7th century CE during Harsha’s reign. He wrote "Si-Yu-Ki," giving detailed accounts of Indian polity and Buddhism.

GK.q: "Tripitakas" are sacred texts of which religion?
GK.e: The Tripitakas (Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka) are Buddhist canonical texts. They were first compiled during the First Buddhist Council.

GK.q: The term "Upanishads" are part of which literature?
GK.e: The Upanishads are philosophical texts forming the end portion of the Vedas, dealing with ultimate reality and the soul.

GK.q: "Megaliths" are associated with which culture in ancient India?
GK.e: Megaliths are large stone structures used for burial practices in South India during the Iron Age. They are found in sites like Maski, Brahmagiri, and Adichanallur.

GK.q: Ashoka’s inscriptions were written in which scripts?
GK.e: Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were in Brahmi script (in Prakrit language). In the northwest, they were in Kharosthi script.

GK.q: The Jatakas are stories associated with
GK.e: Jatakas are Buddhist stories narrating the previous lives of the Buddha, teaching moral values. They are important sources of Buddhist culture.

GK.q: The earliest Tamil literature is known as
GK.e: Sangam literature was composed in Tamil between 300 BCE – 300 CE. It consists of poems on love, war, politics, and society, compiled by assemblies of poets (Sangams).

GK.q: The system of land measurement during the Gupta period was known as
GK.e: Kulyavapa was a unit of land measurement used during the Gupta period, showing advanced agrarian administration.

GK.q: The famous Ellora caves are associated with which religions?
GK.e: Ellora caves (Maharashtra) represent religious harmony. They house Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain caves, built between the 6th–10th centuries CE.

GK.q: Who issued the first gold coins in India?
GK.e: The Indo-Greeks were the first to issue gold coins in India, followed by the Kushans and Guptas who made them more common.

GK.q: Nalanda University was founded by which ruler?
GK.e: Nalanda University (Bihar) was founded by Kumaragupta I of the Gupta dynasty in the 5th century CE. It became a famous Buddhist learning center visited by Hiuen Tsang and I-Tsing.

GK.q: India reduced GST on essential items like toothpaste and life insurance in 2025 in response to rising U.S. tariffs.
GK.e: In 2025, India slashed GST on essentials to 5% and removed levies on insurance and electronics to mitigate impact of steep U.S. tariffs.

GK.q: India initiated “Operation Brahma” in response to an earthquake in which country?
GK.e: Operation Brahma was launched in March 2025 after a major earthquake in Myanmar; India dispatched medical and rescue teams.

GK.q: What milestone event occurred at the 2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh Mela?
GK.e: The 2025 Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj saw over 66 crore people bathing, making it the largest gathering recorded.

GK.q: The National Sports Governance Act 2025 aims to reform governance in which sector?
GK.e: The Act provides a statutory framework for recognition, accountability, and ethics in national sports bodies.

GK.q: “Operation Abhyaas,” a nationwide civil defence mock drill, was conducted in which year?
GK.e: Organized by MHA/NDMA on 7 May 2025, Operation Abhyaas simulated air raids and blackout drills across 244 districts.

GK.q: During the 2025 Tianjin SCO Summit, which three leaders pledged deeper cooperation?
GK.e: Modi, Xi Jinping, and Putin signaled unity and countered geopolitical isolation amid rising U.S. pressure.

GK.q: The April 22, 2025 terrorist attack in Pahalgam led to which Indian military operation?
GK.e: After the attack, India retaliated with missile strikes in Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.

GK.q: India established 108 immigration posts in 2025, including 23 in which region?
GK.e: MHA set up 108 official border posts, 23 of which are in the sensitive Northeast region.

GK.q: Ukraine asked India to take a more proactive role in 2025 for ending hostilities. Who expressed this?
GK.e: Ukraine’s FM requested greater Indian diplomatic engagement in ending the conflict.

GK.q: What was India’s response after engaging with Taliban representatives in 2025?
GK.e: MEA stressed continued engagement as pragmatic policy, but no formal recognition was granted.

GK.q: In 2025, India pushed for a swift Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with which entity?
GK.e: EAM Jaishankar emphasized decisive progress in negotiations of the India–EU FTA.

GK.q: India’s First G20 Summit post-pandemic saw emphasis on revising electoral representation. This is referred to as:
GK.e: The looming end of the seat freeze in 2026 triggered political debate over delimitation’s impact.

GK.q: India hosted the Rising Northeast Investors Summit in May 2025. Where was it held?
GK.e: The summit took place at Bharat Mandapam, promoting Northeast India as an investment hub.

GK.q: What blend level of ethanol in gasoline is India aiming for by 2025–26?
GK.e: India allowed ethanol production from sugarcane juice and molasses to support its 20% blending target.

GK.q: The Asia Cup 2025 is scheduled to begin on which date?
GK.e: Asia Cup 2025 (T20 format) kicks off on 9 September with India–Pakistan fixtures.

GK.q: Which persisted despite other changes: India’s response to anti-immigrant protests in Australia focused on?
GK.e: MEA emphasized that the safety of Indian citizens abroad remained a priority.

GK.q: India’s MHA designated how many railway stations as immigration entry/exit points in 2025?
GK.e: While land, air, and water ports were added, no Northeast railway stations were designated.

GK.q: Who vetoed a U.S.–India trade deal by insisting India reduce Russian oil imports?
GK.e: Trump rejected trade negotiations unless India reduced reliance on Russian oil, creating tensions.

GK.q: In 2025, India began recalibrating GST policy. This was in response to:
GK.e: GST cuts were introduced to cushion Indian consumers and businesses from U.S. protectionism.

GK.q: At the 2025 SCO Summit, which country did Modi meet alongside Xi and Putin?
GK.e: The triangular emphasis was on India, China, and Russia; North Korea did not participate directly.

GK.q: Which event in 2025 saw India rolling out air raid sirens and evacuation exercises?
GK.e: Operation Abhyaas simulated large-scale civil defence preparedness across 244 districts.

GK.q: What motivates neighboring countries to view India’s new immigration posts as beneficial?
GK.e: Immigration posts, especially in Northeast, support tourism and legal cross-border commerce.

GK.q: Which act offers a legal governance structure to India’s sports bodies?
GK.e: This Act standardizes governance, ethics, and accountability in Indian sports.

GK.q: The diplomatic shift at the 2025 Kumbh Mela showcased India’s strengths. Which alignment made it unique?
opts: A rare astrological alignment after 144 years
GK.e: The 2025 Maha Kumbh occurred after a rare planetary configuration—once every 144 years.

GK.q: Which minister introduced the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill in 2025?
GK.e: The bill, introduced in August 2025, allows removal of PMs/CMs detained for 30 days on grave charges.

GK.q: India launched “Bharat Kavach” in 2025. What is it?
GK.e: Bharat Kavach is India’s upgraded indigenous missile defense shield developed to intercept hostile projectiles at long range.

GK.q: Which country became India’s top trading partner in early 2025 despite tariff tensions?
GK.e: Despite disputes, U.S. continued as India’s largest trade partner due to services exports and tech trade.

GK.q: Who won the **2025 Australian Open Men’s Singles title**?
GK.e: Jannik Sinner claimed his first Grand Slam title in 2025 at the Australian Open, defeating Daniil Medvedev.

GK.q: In 2025, India signed a deal with which country to build six nuclear reactors at Jaitapur?
GK.e: India and France moved forward with EDF’s plan for six nuclear reactors at Jaitapur in Maharashtra.

GK.q: Which Indian city was named the **world’s most polluted** in 2024?
GK.e: According to IQAir 2024 report, Delhi again topped the list of world’s most polluted capitals.

GK.q: In April 2025, which country did India surpass to become the **world’s 4th largest stock market** by value?
GK.e: India’s booming equities overtook Japan, placing it behind only U.S., China, and Hong Kong.

GK.q: India’s Chandrayaan-4 mission, approved in 2025, will focus on what?
GK.e: Chandrayaan-4 is planned as India’s first lunar sample return mission in collaboration with JAXA.

GK.q: Who became the **President of Indonesia** in 2024?
GK.e: Defence Minister Prabowo won the 2024 election and took office in 2024.

GK.q: Who is the current **Chief Justice of India (CJI) in 2025**?
GK.e: Justice Sanjiv Khanna took over as CJI in November 2024 after Justice Chandrachud.

GK.q: In 2025, India overtook which country as the **world’s 3rd largest energy consumer**?
GK.e: With rising demand, India became the third-largest energy consumer after China and U.S.

GK.q: The “PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana” launched in 2024 provides what benefit?
opts: Free 300 units of solar power per household
Free rooftop panels to all industries
GK.e: The scheme provides rooftop solar systems and 300 units of free electricity monthly to households.

GK.q: The **ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2024** was won by
GK.e: India won the T20 World Cup 2024, defeating South Africa in the final—ending a 17-year drought.

GK.q: India hosted the **BRICS Summit 2025** in which city?
GK.e: India was the host of the 2025 BRICS Summit, focusing on expanding cooperation with new members.

GK.q: In 2025, which country was admitted as a full member of BRICS?
GK.e: Saudi Arabia joined BRICS alongside UAE and Egypt in the 2024–2025 expansion round.

GK.q: The **Rohini satellite series** launched by ISRO in 2025 focuses on
GK.e: Rohini series satellites provide high-resolution images for environment and agriculture monitoring.

GK.q: Which Indian state hosted the **Khelo India University Games 2024**?
GK.e: UP hosted the 3rd Khelo India University Games across Lucknow, Varanasi, and Gorakhpur.

GK.q: The **2025 Republic Day Chief Guest** was
GK.e: French President Emmanuel Macron attended as the chief guest in January 2025.

GK.q: Who won the **2025 Miss Universe crown**?
GK.e: Anntonia Porsild from Thailand won Miss Universe 2025.

GK.q: The **World’s Tallest Railway Bridge** inaugurated in 2024 is located in
GK.e: Chenab Bridge in J&K is the world’s tallest railway bridge, higher than Eiffel Tower.

GK.q: The **B20 Summit India 2024** (Business 20) was held in
GK.e: The B20 Summit was hosted in Gurugram under India’s G20 presidency.

GK.q: Which is India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier commissioned in 2022 and active in 2024–25?
GK.e: INS Vikrant is India’s first indigenously built aircraft carrier, commissioned in 2022.

GK.q: India’s digital currency project, **e-Rupee**, is managed by
GK.e: RBI launched the pilot for CBDC—digital rupee—for wholesale and retail use.

GK.q: The **Global Climate Summit 2024 (COP29)** was held in
GK.e: COP29 climate talks were hosted by Azerbaijan in Baku in 2024.

GK.q: Which state topped India’s **Ease of Doing Business rankings 2024**?
GK.e: Andhra Pradesh topped the national ease of doing business rankings for 2024.

GK.q: Who won the **2025 Grammy for Best Global Music Album**?
GK.e: Indian singer Shankar Mahadevan, part of “Shakti,” won Grammy in 2025.

GK.q: In 2025, India unveiled the **BharatGPT consortium**. Its purpose is
opts: Large language model in Indian languages
GK.e: BharatGPT aims to create AI models for Indian languages, competing with ChatGPT.

GK.q: The **2025 Women’s Cricket World Cup** is scheduled to be hosted in
GK.e: India will host the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup in 2025.

GK.q: India’s tallest statue in 2024 after the Statue of Unity is
GK.e: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Memorial in Mumbai became India’s second-tallest statue.

GK.q: Which Indian bank launched “Digital Rupee Wallet” in 2024?
GK.e: State Bank of India introduced its digital rupee wallet under RBI’s CBDC initiative.

GK.q: The **Nobel Peace Prize 2024** was awarded to
GK.e: Nobel Committee honored activists from Iran’s women’s movement for fighting oppression.

GK.q: India’s first underwater metro was inaugurated in 2024 in
GK.e: Kolkata Metro introduced India’s first underwater metro tunnel under the Hooghly river.

GK.q: India’s GDP growth rate projection for FY 2025 by IMF is
GK.e: IMF forecasted India’s GDP growth for FY25 at 6.8%, making it the fastest-growing major economy.

GK.q: The **2025 World Expo** is being hosted by
GK.e: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is hosting World Expo 2025 with sustainability and technology themes.

GK.q: Which gas is primarily responsible for global warming?
GK.e: CO₂ is the major greenhouse gas responsible for global warming, though methane and nitrous oxide are also significant contributors.

GK.q: The Kyoto Protocol is related to
GK.e: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) was the first international treaty to set legally binding targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

GK.q: The major cause of acid rain is
GK.e: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides mix with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid, leading to acid rain.

GK.q: The headquarters of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) is located in
GK.e: IUCN is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland, and maintains the Red List of Threatened Species.

GK.q: Which protocol banned the use of CFCs to protect the ozone layer?
GK.e: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out ozone-depleting substances like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

GK.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
GK.e: Solar, wind, tidal, and geothermal energy are renewable sources, unlike coal and petroleum which are non-renewable.

GK.q: Silent Valley movement in Kerala was related to
opts: Prevention of deforestation due to a dam
GK.e: The Silent Valley movement (1970s) opposed a hydroelectric project in Kerala to save tropical evergreen forests.

GK.q: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep global temperature rise this century below
GK.e: The Paris Agreement aims to limit global warming to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C.

GK.q: The Chipko Movement was mainly related to
GK.e: Started in the 1970s in Uttarakhand, villagers hugged trees to prevent them from being cut.

GK.q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas but not controlled by Kyoto Protocol?
GK.e: Water vapour is a natural greenhouse gas and not targeted by Kyoto, unlike CO₂, CH₄, and N₂O.

GK.q: The largest source of air pollution in India is
GK.e: Vehicular emissions are the main source of air pollution in Indian cities, releasing CO, NOx, and particulate matter.

GK.q: The ozone hole is mainly found over
GK.e: Ozone depletion is most severe over Antarctica due to polar stratospheric clouds and low temperatures.

GK.q: Which country hosted the COP28 Climate Summit (2023)?
GK.e: COP28 was hosted by the United Arab Emirates in Dubai, focusing on climate finance and renewable energy.

GK.q: The "Blue Flag" certification is given to
GK.e: Blue Flag certification is awarded internationally to beaches and marinas that meet high standards of cleanliness and safety.

GK.q: Which of the following gases has the highest global warming potential (GWP)?
GK.e: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) have very high GWP compared to CO₂ and CH₄, making them highly damaging.

GK.q: The Ramsar Convention is related to
GK.e: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.

GK.q: Which Indian city launched the "Odd-Even Scheme" to reduce pollution?
GK.e: The Delhi Government launched the odd-even scheme for vehicles to control severe air pollution levels.

GK.q: Which Indian state launched the "Green Hydrogen Policy" in 2022?
GK.e: Rajasthan launched India’s first Green Hydrogen Policy, encouraging renewable hydrogen production.

GK.q: The term "carbon footprint" refers to
opts: The amount of greenhouse gases emitted by human activity
The size of carbon deposits in soil
The level of carbon in oceans
GK.e: A carbon footprint measures the total greenhouse gases, especially CO₂, released directly or indirectly by individuals or organizations.

GK.q: Which Indian state has the highest installed capacity of solar power as of 2024?
GK.e: Rajasthan leads in solar power generation in India due to its large desert areas and high solar potential.

GK.q: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable waste?
GK.e: Plastic bags are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment for hundreds of years.

GK.q: The Biodiversity Hotspot "Indo-Burma Region" covers which Indian state?
GK.e: Indo-Burma is one of India’s four biodiversity hotspots, covering northeast India including Mizoram and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

GK.q: The Ganga Action Plan was launched in
GK.e: Ganga Action Plan was launched in 1985 to clean and rejuvenate the Ganga River, but results were limited.

GK.q: Which is the first state in India to implement a State Climate Change Action Plan?
GK.e: Himachal Pradesh was the first state to prepare and implement a climate change action plan in 2009.

GK.q: The Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) is headquartered in
GK.e: ZSI, established in 1916, conducts surveys of fauna and maintains data on Indian animal biodiversity.

GK.q: Which year was declared by the UN as the "International Year of Millets"?
GK.e: The UN declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets, led by India to promote sustainable agriculture.

GK.q: The main pollutant responsible for Minamata disease is
GK.e: Minamata disease was caused by mercury poisoning due to industrial wastewater discharge in Japan.

GK.q: The "Green Credit Programme" launched by the Indian Government in 2023 is related to
GK.e: The Green Credit Programme incentivizes individuals and organizations to take up tree plantation and environmental activities.

GK.q: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in
GK.e: The NGT was established in 2010 to provide speedy redressal of environmental disputes.

GK.q: Which Indian city ranked as the most polluted city in the world in 2023 according to IQAir report?
GK.e: Delhi was ranked as the most polluted city globally in 2023 due to severe smog, vehicular emissions, and crop burning.

GK.q: Who is regarded as the “Father of Indian Economic Planning”?
GK.e: M. Visvesvaraya proposed the concept of economic planning in his book “Planned Economy for India” (1934).

GK.q: The concept of “Mixed Economy” in India refers to
opts: Both public and private sectors co-exist
GK.e: India adopted a mixed economy model where both private and public sectors play a significant role.

GK.q: Which was the first Five-Year Plan in India?
GK.e: India’s first Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused mainly on agriculture, irrigation, and energy.

GK.q: National Income of India is estimated by
GK.e: The CSO (now part of NSO) estimates national income through various surveys and statistics.

GK.q: Which of the following is NOT a direct tax in India?
GK.e: GST is an indirect tax levied on consumption of goods and services, not directly on income.

GK.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in
GK.e: RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, as the central bank of India.

GK.q: Who presents the Union Budget in the Parliament?
GK.e: As per Article 112, the Finance Minister presents the Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) in Lok Sabha.

GK.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India on
GK.e: GST, India’s biggest indirect tax reform, was launched on 1 July 2017.

GK.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India’s GDP? (as of 2025)
GK.e: The services sector contributes over 50% to India’s GDP, led by IT, banking, and telecom.

GK.q: The “Green Revolution” in India was associated with
GK.e: Green Revolution (1960s–70s) led by M. S. Swaminathan focused on high-yield variety seeds and irrigation.

GK.q: Which Indian economist gave the concept of “Poverty Line”?
GK.e: Dadabhai Naoroji’s “Drain Theory” and poverty line estimates are pioneering contributions in Indian economy.

GK.q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees employment for
GK.e: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households.

GK.q: The repo rate is the rate at which
opts: RBI lends money to commercial banks
GK.e: Repo rate is the short-term lending rate of RBI to control liquidity and inflation.

GK.q: Which scheme was launched to provide LPG connections to women from BPL households?
GK.e: Launched in 2016, the scheme provides free LPG connections to women from poor households.

GK.q: Which Indian economist won the Nobel Prize in Economics?
GK.e: Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in 1998 for his work on welfare economics and poverty.

GK.q: The disinvestment of Public Sector Enterprises in India is handled by
opts: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
GK.e: DIPAM manages disinvestment of government equity in public sector undertakings.

GK.q: The largest producer of milk in the world is
GK.e: India is the largest milk producer globally, contributing about 24% of world milk production.

GK.q: “Operation Flood” is related to
GK.e: Operation Flood launched in 1970 made India the world’s largest producer of milk.

GK.q: Who regulates the stock exchanges in India?
GK.e: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates stock markets and protects investors.

GK.q: Which state is the largest producer of wheat in India?
GK.e: Uttar Pradesh is the largest wheat-producing state, followed by Punjab and Madhya Pradesh.

GK.q: The Economic Survey of India is published by
GK.e: The Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance publishes the Economic Survey annually before the Budget.

GK.q: The base year for India’s GDP calculation (as of 2025) is
GK.e: Currently, India uses 2011–12 as the base year for GDP estimation. Work is ongoing to update it.

GK.q: Which is the largest employment provider sector in India?
GK.e: Agriculture remains the largest employer in India, though services contribute more to GDP.

GK.q: The currency of India is issued by
GK.e: Except ₹1 notes and coins (issued by Finance Ministry), all currency notes are issued by RBI.

GK.q: Who was the Finance Minister of India when GST was introduced in 2017?
GK.e: Arun Jaitley was the Finance Minister during the introduction of GST in July 2017.

GK.q: “Fiscal Deficit” refers to
GK.e: Fiscal deficit is the gap between total expenditure and total non-borrowed receipts.

GK.q: Which institution releases the “Human Development Report”?
GK.e: The United Nations Development Programme publishes the Human Development Report annually.

GK.q: What does “MSP” stand for in Indian economy?
GK.e: MSP is the minimum price guaranteed by the government to farmers for their crops.

GK.q: In 2024–25, India’s GDP growth rate is projected around
GK.e: As per IMF and RBI estimates, India’s GDP is projected to grow around 6.5% in 2024–25.

GK.q: Which bank launched India’s first digital currency pilot program in 2022?
GK.e: The Reserve Bank of India launched a pilot project for Digital Rupee (CBDC) in 2022.

GK.q: Which committee recommended the LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) reforms in India?
GK.e: The Narasimham Committee (1991) recommended financial sector reforms leading to LPG policies.

GK.q: Which organization publishes the “World Development Report”?
GK.e: The World Bank annually publishes the “World Development Report” focusing on global economic issues.

GK.q: Which state in India is known as the “Rice Bowl of India”?
GK.e: Andhra Pradesh is called the Rice Bowl due to high rice production supported by irrigation.

GK.q: What is the main objective of “Startup India” launched in 2016?
GK.e: Startup India aims to promote innovation and startups through tax benefits, easier funding, and policies.

GK.q: In India, disinvestment policy was first adopted in which year?
GK.e: Disinvestment of PSUs was introduced during economic reforms in 1991 to reduce fiscal deficit.

GK.q: “Jan Dhan Yojana” is related to
GK.e: PMJDY launched in 2014 aims to provide banking facilities, insurance, and debit cards to the unbanked.

GK.q: Who presents the “Economic Survey” in Parliament before the Union Budget?
GK.e: The CEA prepares and presents the Economic Survey, which reviews the past year’s economy.

GK.q: Which index measures inflation at the wholesale level in India?
GK.e: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) tracks price changes at the wholesale market level in India.

GK.q: The “Blue Revolution” is related to
GK.e: Blue Revolution refers to the rapid development of fisheries and aquaculture in India.

GK.q: The “Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan” launched in 2020 primarily focuses on
GK.e: Atmanirbhar Bharat aims to make India self-reliant by boosting local production and reducing imports.

GK.q: What is the current repo rate of RBI as of January 2025?
GK.e: RBI has kept the repo rate steady at 6.5% since February 2023 to control inflation.

GK.q: The “Golden Quadrilateral Project” is related to
GK.e: Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata with express highways.

GK.q: In which year was the Planning Commission replaced by NITI Aayog?
GK.e: On 1 January 2015, NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission as the new think tank.

GK.q: India’s first Post Office Savings Bank Payment Bank was launched in
GK.e: IPPB was launched nationwide in 2018 to promote financial inclusion using postal networks.

GK.q: “Mudra Bank” provides loans to
GK.e: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana offers loans to small businesses up to ₹10 lakh.

GK.q: The “Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT)” in India is applicable on
GK.e: MAT ensures that companies pay a minimum amount of tax even if they show low profits.

GK.q: Which is the largest contributor of FDI inflows in India (2023–24)?
GK.e: Singapore has been the top source of FDI in India, followed by USA and Mauritius.

GK.q: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana is related to
GK.e: PMKSY was launched in 2015 to improve irrigation and water-use efficiency.

GK.q: Which institution regulates insurance companies in India?
GK.e: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates insurance companies.

GK.q: What is India’s unemployment rate (approx) in 2024 as per CMIE?
GK.e: CMIE reported India’s unemployment rate around 7.5% in late 2024.

GK.q: Which programme guarantees food security by providing food grains at subsidized rates?
GK.e: National Food Security Act (2013) provides subsidized food grains to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population.

GK.q: The “Twin Balance Sheet Problem” in India refers to
opts: Current account deficit and fiscal deficit
GK.e: The problem refers to high NPAs of banks and debt-ridden corporates.

GK.q: In India, who issues coins?
GK.e: Coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance, while RBI issues currency notes.

GK.q: What does “NEFT” stand for in banking?
GK.e: NEFT allows one-to-one fund transfer electronically between bank accounts.

GK.q: India’s largest trading partner (2024) is
GK.e: USA is India’s largest trading partner, followed by China and UAE.

GK.q: Which scheme replaced the Planning Commission’s 12th Five-Year Plan?
GK.e: NITI Aayog introduced a 15-year Vision, 7-year strategy, and 3-year action agenda instead of 5-year plans.

GK.q: The “Poverty Estimation Committee” chaired in 2011 was
GK.e: C. Rangarajan Committee re-estimated poverty lines in 2011 after the Tendulkar methodology.

GK.q: The currency notes in India are signed by
GK.e: All currency notes (except ₹1 note signed by Finance Secretary) are signed by RBI Governor.

GK.q: As per Budget 2024, the highest allocation among ministries was for
GK.e: Defence sector received the largest allocation in the 2024 Union Budget.

GK.q: India’s rank in the World Bank’s “Ease of Doing Business Report 2020” (last edition) was
GK.e: India ranked 63rd in the World Bank’s Ease of Doing Business Report 2020, the final edition before discontinuation.

GK.q: Which is the longest river in India?
GK.e: The Ganga is the longest river in India, flowing about 2525 km from the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand to the Bay of Bengal.

GK.q: The southernmost point of India is
GK.e: Indira Point, located in the Nicobar Islands, is the southernmost point of India. It was submerged during the 2004 tsunami but remains geographically significant.

GK.q: The largest delta in the world is
GK.e: The Sundarbans Delta, formed by the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, is the world’s largest delta, famous for its mangrove forests and Royal Bengal Tigers.

GK.q: Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
GK.e: Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

GK.q: The largest state of India by area is
GK.e: Rajasthan is the largest state by area, covering 342,239 sq km, while Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state.

GK.q: The highest peak in India is
GK.e: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest mountain peak in India, located on the border of Sikkim and Nepal. Mount Everest lies entirely in Nepal/Tibet.

GK.q: The longest dam in India is
GK.e: Hirakud Dam, built across the Mahanadi River in Odisha, is the longest dam in India, extending about 25.8 km including dykes.

GK.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
GK.e: Wular Lake, located in Jammu & Kashmir, is the largest freshwater lake in India. It was formed due to tectonic activity.

GK.q: The highest waterfall in India is
GK.e: Nohkalikai Falls in Meghalaya is the highest plunge waterfall in India with a height of 340 m.

GK.q: The standard meridian of India passes through
GK.e: The standard meridian of India (82.5°E) passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh and is used to set IST (Indian Standard Time).

GK.q: The Deccan Plateau is made up of
GK.e: The Deccan Plateau was formed by volcanic activity around 65 million years ago, consisting mainly of basalt igneous rocks.

GK.q: The largest saltwater lake in India is
GK.e: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest saltwater lagoon in India and the second-largest in the world. It is a Ramsar wetland site.

GK.q: Which river is called the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
GK.e: The Kosi River is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar" due to frequent flooding and devastation caused in the region.

GK.q: The Silent Valley National Park is located in
GK.e: Silent Valley National Park, located in Kerala, is famous for its evergreen tropical forests and endangered lion-tailed macaque.

GK.q: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at
GK.e: The Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu are the meeting point of the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats.

GK.q: The largest port in India by volume of cargo handled is
GK.e: Kandla Port (now called Deendayal Port) in Gujarat is the largest by volume of cargo handled, especially petroleum products.

GK.q: Siachen Glacier is located in
GK.e: Siachen Glacier, located in the eastern Karakoram Range, is the highest battlefield in the world, controlled by India.

GK.q: The westernmost longitude of India is
GK.e: The westernmost point of India is Ghuar Mota in Gujarat, at longitude 68°7′E.

GK.q: Which is the deepest river valley in India?
GK.e: The Narmada River forms one of the deepest gorges in India, flowing between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

GK.q: The largest coal-producing state in India is
GK.e: Jharkhand is the largest coal-producing state in India, accounting for more than 25% of total production.

GK.q: The only floating national park in the world is
GK.e: Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur is the only floating national park in the world, famous for Sangai deer.

GK.q: The western coastal plain of India is also known as
GK.e: The western coastal plain has two parts: Konkan Coast (north) and Malabar Coast (south).

GK.q: The longest national highway in India is
GK.e: NH-44 is the longest national highway in India, stretching from Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu).

GK.q: Loktak Lake is famous for
GK.e: Loktak Lake in Manipur is famous for floating vegetation masses called "Phumdis."

GK.q: The Satpura Range is located in
GK.e: The Satpura Range lies in central India, mainly in Madhya Pradesh, forming part of the Deccan Plateau.

GK.q: The "Seven Sisters" states of India are located in
GK.e: The "Seven Sisters" are Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura.

GK.q: The only state in India where golden langur is found is
GK.e: Golden langurs are an endangered species found only in western Assam and parts of Bhutan.

GK.q: Which river originates from Amarkantak Plateau?
GK.e: Both Narmada and Son rivers originate from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh.

GK.q: The Gir Forest in Gujarat is famous for
GK.e: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the world.

GK.q: The Constitution of India came into force on
GK.e: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into effect on 26 January 1950 to mark the Purna Swaraj Declaration of 1930.

GK.q: Who is regarded as the “Father of the Indian Constitution”?
GK.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee, played the most significant role in framing the Constitution.

GK.q: The concept of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from
GK.e: Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Bill of Rights in the US Constitution.

GK.q: The President of India is elected by
opts: Elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies
Both Houses of Parliament and Governors
GK.e: The President is elected indirectly through an electoral college consisting of elected MPs and MLAs.

GK.q: Who was the first President of India?
GK.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the first President of India (1950–1962).

GK.q: The idea of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) has been borrowed from
GK.e: DPSPs were influenced by the Irish Constitution, inspired by Gandhian philosophy.

GK.q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
GK.e: The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners under Article 324.

GK.q: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in the Indian Constitution?
GK.e: Originally 10 were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976); the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more, making it 11.

GK.q: The Supreme Court of India was established in
GK.e: The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, replacing the Federal Court of India.

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes “Untouchability”?
GK.e: Article 17 prohibits untouchability and makes its practice an offense.

GK.q: How many Schedules are there in the Indian Constitution (as of 2024)?
GK.e: The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; currently, there are 12 after amendments.

GK.q: Who presides over the joint sitting of Parliament?
GK.e: The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings of both Houses under Article 118.

GK.q: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
GK.e: The 61st Amendment Act (1988) reduced the voting age to 18 years.

GK.q: Which Article deals with the impeachment of the President of India?
GK.e: Article 61 provides the procedure for impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution.

GK.q: Money Bill can be introduced only in
GK.e: Article 110 states that a Money Bill can only be introduced in Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.

GK.q: Which High Court has the largest jurisdiction in India?
GK.e: Bombay High Court has jurisdiction over Maharashtra, Goa, Daman & Diu, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli.

GK.q: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
GK.e: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Supreme Court judge in 1989.

GK.q: Which Constitutional body publishes the “Union and State Audit Reports”?
GK.e: The CAG audits Union and State government accounts and presents reports to legislatures.

GK.q: Panchayati Raj was first introduced in India in
GK.e: Panchayati Raj was first introduced in 1959 at Nagaur, Rajasthan.

GK.q: Which Fundamental Right cannot be suspended during Emergency?
opts: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
GK.e: Article 21 cannot be suspended even during an Emergency (44th Amendment, 1978).

GK.q: Who is known as the guardian of the Indian Constitution?
GK.e: The Supreme Court ensures the Constitution is upheld through judicial review.

GK.q: In which year was the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (Panchayati Raj) passed?
GK.e: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992, gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

GK.q: The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill for a maximum of
GK.e: Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill but must return it within 14 days.

GK.q: The Anti-Defection Law was enacted in India through which amendment?
GK.e: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, added the Anti-Defection Law under the Tenth Schedule.

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution declares India as a secular state?
GK.e: The word “Secular” was added in the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

GK.q: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
GK.e: The Chief Justice administers the oath; in his absence, the senior-most judge does so.

GK.q: The NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in
GK.e: NITI Aayog was formed in 2015 as a policy think-tank, replacing the Planning Commission.

GK.q: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha?
GK.e: The President nominates 12 members with expertise in art, science, literature, and social service.

GK.q: The first Lok Sabha elections were held in
GK.e: The first general elections were held in 1951–52, with Congress emerging victorious.

GK.q: Which part of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights?
GK.e: Fundamental Rights are mentioned in Part III (Articles 12–35).

GK.q: Which Constitutional body recently recommended simultaneous elections in India (2024 report)?
GK.e: The 22nd Law Commission in 2024 recommended “One Nation, One Election” for efficiency.

GK.q: The 105th Constitutional Amendment (2021) is related to
GK.e: The 105th Amendment restores the states’ power to identify OBCs for reservation.

GK.q: Which Supreme Court judgment declared “Right to Privacy” as a Fundamental Right?
opts: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
K. S. Puttaswamy vs. Union of India
GK.e: In 2017, SC declared Right to Privacy as part of Article 21.

GK.q: In 2023, which Bill was passed to replace the colonial-era IPC, CrPC, and Evidence Act?
opts: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, Bharatiya Sakshya Bill
GK.e: These 3 Bills, passed in 2023, aim to modernize criminal laws in India.

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution gives the right to Constitutional Remedies?
GK.e: Article 32 allows citizens to move the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights.

GK.q: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
GK.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel served as India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and also the first Home Minister, known as the “Iron Man of India.”

GK.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of life and personal liberty?
GK.e: Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, which cannot be taken away except according to procedure established by law.

GK.q: Who has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha before the completion of its term?
GK.e: The President can dissolve Lok Sabha on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

GK.q: Which Constitutional Amendment made Right to Education a Fundamental Right?
GK.e: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children (6–14 years) a Fundamental Right.

GK.q: The President of India addresses both Houses of Parliament assembled together at
opts: The beginning of the first session of each year and at first session after every general election
GK.e: As per Article 87, the President addresses Parliament at the start of the first session every year and after each general election.

GK.q: The concept of Judicial Review in India is derived from the Constitution of
GK.e: Judicial Review in India is inspired by the US system, allowing the judiciary to review laws and executive actions for constitutionality.

GK.q: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is
GK.e: Article 81 provides that the maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 552 (530 from states, 20 from Union Territories, and 2 nominated from Anglo-Indians—though the nomination provision has now been removed).

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of Finance Commission?
GK.e: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every 5 years to recommend distribution of revenues between Centre and States.

GK.q: Who presides over the Rajya Sabha?
GK.e: The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

GK.q: Which amendment is known as the “Mini Constitution” of India?
GK.e: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, made sweeping changes to the Constitution, hence called the “Mini Constitution.”

GK.q: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian state?
GK.e: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian state (Uttar Pradesh, 1947–49).

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency?
GK.e: Article 359 allows the suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21) during a National Emergency.

GK.q: Who appoints the Governor of a State?
GK.e: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President under Article 155.

GK.q: Which Commission recommended the reorganization of States on linguistic basis?
GK.e: The States Reorganization Commission (1953–55) recommended reorganization of states based on linguistic and administrative convenience.

GK.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
GK.e: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was the first Speaker of Lok Sabha (1952–1956).

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution mentions the post of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)?
GK.e: Article 148 provides for the appointment of CAG, who audits Union and State government accounts.

GK.q: Who has the power to decide disputes relating to the election of the President of India?
GK.e: Any dispute regarding the election of the President is decided exclusively by the Supreme Court under Article 71.

GK.q: Which constitutional body was established by the 97th Constitutional Amendment?
GK.e: The 97th Amendment (2011) gave constitutional status to Cooperative Societies, inserting Article 43B and Part IXB.

GK.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the NITI Aayog?
GK.e: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog.

GK.q: In which year did India adopt the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
GK.e: GST was launched on 1 July 2017 as India’s biggest tax reform, replacing multiple indirect taxes.

GK.q: In 2024, which state became the first in India to implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC)?
GK.e: Uttarakhand became the first state (2024) to pass a Uniform Civil Code covering marriage, divorce, succession, and live-in relationships.

GK.q: Who is the present Chief Justice of India (as of September 2025)?
GK.e: Justice D. Y. Chandrachud is the 50th Chief Justice of India, appointed in November 2022.

GK.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the official language of India?
GK.e: Article 343 states that Hindi in Devanagari script shall be the official language of the Union.

GK.q: Which committee recommended the Panchayati Raj system in India?
GK.e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the establishment of Panchayati Raj Institutions in India.

GK.q: In 2025, which country signed a new defence pact with India, strengthening Indo-Pacific security cooperation?
GK.e: In early 2025, India and Australia signed a comprehensive defence pact to enhance maritime security and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

GK.q: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj?
GK.e: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828. It aimed to reform Hindu society by opposing idol worship, caste distinctions, and promoting monotheism.

GK.q: The "Doctrine of Lapse" was introduced by
GK.e: Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856) introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, under which states without a male heir were annexed by the British. Jhansi, Satara, and Nagpur were annexed this way.

GK.q: Who was the founder of the Arya Samaj?
GK.e: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875. He emphasized "Back to the Vedas" and opposed child marriage, idol worship, and caste discrimination.

GK.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in
GK.e: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 at Bombay. The first session was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee and attended by 72 delegates.

GK.q: The Partition of Bengal was carried out in
GK.e: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal on 16 October 1905, citing administrative efficiency. However, it was aimed at weakening nationalism. It was annulled in 1911 due to strong protests.

GK.q: Who gave the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
GK.e: Tilak, a leader of the extremist wing of the Congress, popularized the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright" during the freedom struggle.

GK.q: The Khilafat Movement was led by
GK.e: The Khilafat Movement (1919–1924) was led by Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali to protect the Khalifa’s position in Turkey. Gandhi supported it to unite Hindus and Muslims.

GK.q: Who started the Aligarh Movement?
GK.e: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Aligarh Movement to promote modern education among Muslims. He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875, later Aligarh Muslim University.

GK.q: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Revolt of 1857?
GK.e: Lord Canning was the Viceroy during the Revolt of 1857, also called the First War of Independence. He later passed the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858 transferring power from the East India Company to the British Crown.

GK.q: The Simon Commission was appointed in
GK.e: The Simon Commission was appointed in 1927 to review the Government of India Act, 1919. It was boycotted by Indians because it had no Indian members.

GK.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in
GK.e: On 13 April 1919, General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, killing hundreds. This brutal event shocked the nation and strengthened the independence struggle.

GK.q: Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience Movement with the
GK.e: Gandhi began the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the famous Dandi March, where he broke the salt law by making salt from seawater at Dandi, Gujarat.

GK.q: The Indian Independence League was formed by
GK.e: Rash Behari Bose formed the Indian Independence League in Japan. Later, Subhas Chandra Bose took leadership and formed the Indian National Army (INA).

GK.q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
GK.e: Lord Mountbatten served as the first Governor-General of independent India (1947–48). He was succeeded by C. Rajagopalachari, the first Indian Governor-General.

GK.q: Who founded the Indian National Army (INA)?
GK.e: The INA was initially formed by Captain Mohan Singh with Japanese support during World War II. Subhas Chandra Bose later reorganized it and gave the call "Chalo Dilli."

GK.q: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of independence in 1947?
GK.e: J.B. Kripalani was the INC President in 1947. He played an important role in the transfer of power negotiations.

GK.q: Who gave the call "Dilli Chalo"?
GK.e: Subhas Chandra Bose gave the slogan "Dilli Chalo" to his INA soldiers, urging them to capture Delhi from the British during World War II.

GK.q: The "August Offer" was made by
GK.e: The August Offer (1940) was made by Viceroy Linlithgow. It promised dominion status after the war but was rejected by the Congress as inadequate.

GK.q: Who among the following founded the Theosophical Society in India?
GK.e: The Theosophical Society was founded in the USA in 1875 by Blavatsky and Olcott. It shifted headquarters to Adyar, Madras, in 1882. Annie Besant later popularized it in India.

GK.q: Who presided over the historic Lahore Session of Congress in 1929?
GK.e: At the Lahore Session of 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress declared "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) as its goal and observed 26 January 1930 as Independence Day.

GK.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in
GK.e: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942 at Bombay, demanding immediate independence. The slogan was "Do or Die."

GK.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between
GK.e: The Poona Pact between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar ended the fast by Gandhi against separate electorates for Dalits. It reserved seats for depressed classes in legislatures within the general electorate.

GK.q: Who was the founder of the Ramakrishna Mission?
GK.e: Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 in memory of his guru Ramakrishna Paramhansa. It focused on education, social service, and spiritual teachings.

GK.q: Who started the Home Rule Movement in India?
opts: Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Subhas Chandra Bose and Rash Behari Bose
Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale
GK.e: The Home Rule Movement (1916) was started separately by Tilak in Maharashtra and Annie Besant in Madras. It demanded self-rule for India.

GK.q: Who was the Viceroy when the Indian Councils Act of 1892 was passed?
GK.e: The Indian Councils Act, 1892, passed under Lord Lansdowne, increased the number of members in legislative councils and allowed limited discussion of the budget.

GK.q: Who founded the Indian Association in 1876?
GK.e: Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose founded the Indian Association in 1876. It was a forerunner of the Indian National Congress.

GK.q: Who authored "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"?
GK.e: Dadabhai Naoroji, the "Grand Old Man of India," authored this book in which he explained the "Drain of Wealth" theory, showing how British policies drained India’s resources.

GK.q: The Wavell Plan was announced in
GK.e: The Wavell Plan was announced in 1945 by Lord Wavell to resolve constitutional deadlock. It proposed equal representation for caste Hindus and Muslims in the executive council, but it failed.

GK.q: Who was known as the "Frontier Gandhi"?
GK.e: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a Pashtun leader, was called "Frontier Gandhi" for his non-violent struggle against British rule in the North-West Frontier Province. He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement.

GK.q: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
GK.e: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India. After independence, he served as the first Governor-General of India until June 1948.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
GK.e: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to win the Nobel Prize in 1913 for Literature, for his work *Gitanjali*.

GK.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by area?
GK.e: Lake Superior, located in North America, is the largest freshwater lake by surface area. However, by volume, Lake Baikal is the largest.

GK.q: Who is popularly known as the "Iron Man of India"?
GK.e: Sardar Patel is called the "Iron Man of India" for his leadership in uniting princely states into modern India after independence.

GK.q: The Bharat Ratna is awarded for exceptional service in which fields?
GK.e: The Bharat Ratna is India’s highest civilian award, given for exceptional service in any field of human achievement.

GK.q: Who won the first individual Olympic gold medal for India?
GK.e: Abhinav Bindra won India’s first individual Olympic gold medal in shooting (10m air rifle) at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

GK.q: Which is the longest river in the world?
GK.e: The Nile River in Africa is generally considered the longest river in the world at about 6,650 km, though some studies claim the Amazon is slightly longer.

GK.q: Who is known as the "Nightingale of India"?
GK.e: Sarojini Naidu, a poet and freedom fighter, was called the "Nightingale of India" for her lyrical poetry.

GK.q: Which Indian film won the first Oscar for Best Original Song?
GK.e: "Jai Ho" from *Slumdog Millionaire* won the Oscar for Best Original Song in 2009. In 2023, *RRR*’s "Naatu Naatu" also won.

GK.q: The headquarters of Indian Coast Guard is located at
GK.e: The Indian Coast Guard, responsible for maritime safety and security, has its headquarters in New Delhi.

GK.q: International Women’s Day is celebrated every year on
GK.e: International Women’s Day is celebrated worldwide on 8th March to highlight women’s rights and achievements.

GK.q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of the world?
GK.e: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka became the world’s first woman Prime Minister in 1960.

GK.q: Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
GK.e: Mount Everest, at 8,848.86 m above sea level, is the world’s highest mountain peak.

GK.q: Who is popularly known as the "Flying Sikh"?
GK.e: Milkha Singh, the legendary Indian sprinter, is nicknamed the "Flying Sikh" for his outstanding performances in athletics.

GK.q: Who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 along with Malala Yousafzai?
GK.e: Indian child rights activist Kailash Satyarthi shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai for their fight against child labour and for education.

GK.q: The motto of the Indian Air Force is
GK.e: The motto "Touch the Sky with Glory" (Nabhah Sprisham Deeptam) is taken from the Bhagavad Gita.

GK.q: Which country is called the "Land of Rising Sun"?
GK.e: Japan is called the "Land of Rising Sun" because it is located to the east of Asia where the sun rises first.

GK.q: The first Indian woman to go to space was
GK.e: Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman astronaut who went to space in 1997 on Space Shuttle Columbia.

GK.q: Which is the national sport of India?
GK.e: India has no officially declared national sport, though hockey is often mistaken as one due to its past Olympic achievements.

GK.q: Who is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?

GK.e: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is called the "Missile Man of India" for his role in India’s missile and space programmes.

GK.e: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for her novel *The God of Small Things*.

GK.q: The National Defence Academy (NDA) is located at
GK.e: NDA, India’s premier joint services academy for Army, Navy, and Air Force, is located in Khadakwasla near Pune.

GK.e: World Environment Day is observed on 5th June each year to raise awareness about environmental protection.

GK.e: Vatican City, an independent city-state inside Rome, is the smallest country in the world, with an area of just 0.49 sq km.

GK.e: The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954 to C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, and C.V. Raman.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win the Miss World title?
GK.e: Reita Faria won Miss World in 1966, becoming the first Indian woman to achieve this title.

GK.q: Which is the largest desert in the world?
GK.e: Though covered with ice, Antarctica is classified as the largest desert in the world due to extremely low precipitation.

GK.q: Who is known as the "Grand Old Man of India"?
GK.e: Dadabhai Naoroji was called the "Grand Old Man of India" for his long and dedicated contribution to India’s freedom struggle.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics?
GK.e: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1998 for his work in welfare economics.

GK.q: Which Indian cricketer is nicknamed the "Little Master"?
GK.e: Sunil Gavaskar was known as the "Little Master" for his outstanding batting skills. Sachin Tendulkar was later called "Master Blaster".

GK.q: Which is the largest continent in the world?
GK.e: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of Earth’s total land area and hosting nearly 60% of the world’s population.

GK.q: Who is the first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna?
GK.e: Indira Gandhi, India’s first woman Prime Minister, received the Bharat Ratna in 1971.

GK.q: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
GK.e: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world, covering one-third of Earth’s surface.

GK.q: Who is popularly known as the "Magician of Football"?
GK.e: Pele, the Brazilian football legend, is called the "Magician of Football" for his exceptional skills and records.

GK.q: Who was the first woman President of the United Nations General Assembly?
GK.e: Vijayalakshmi Pandit became the first woman President of the UN General Assembly in 1953.

GK.q: The highest civilian award of the United States is
GK.e: The Presidential Medal of Freedom is the highest civilian award in the USA.

GK.q: Which Indian city is known as the "City of Lakes"?
GK.e: Udaipur in Rajasthan is called the "City of Lakes" due to its numerous beautiful lakes like Pichola, Fateh Sagar, and Jaisamand.

GK.q: Who was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award?
GK.e: Malayalam writer G. Sankara Kurup was the first to receive the Jnanpith Award in 1965 for his work *Odakkuzhal*.

GK.q: The Indian Navy Day is celebrated on
GK.e: Indian Navy Day is observed on 4th December to commemorate Operation Trident during the 1971 Indo-Pak war.

GK.q: Which is the longest railway platform in the world?
GK.e: The Hubballi railway platform in Karnataka is the world’s longest, measuring 1,505 meters.

GK.q: Who is called the "Father of the Indian Constitution"?
GK.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is regarded as the "Father of the Indian Constitution" for his pivotal role as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

GK.q: The Oscar award is presented annually by which academy?
opts: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
GK.e: The Oscars are presented by AMPAS to honour excellence in the film industry.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver medal?
GK.e: P.V. Sindhu won a silver medal in badminton at the 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to achieve this feat.

GK.q: Which is the tallest statue in the world?
GK.e: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, at 182 m, is the tallest statue in the world.

GK.q: Who is known as the "Human Computer"?
GK.e: Indian mathematician Shakuntala Devi is called the "Human Computer" for her extraordinary calculation abilities.

GK.q: The Nobel Prize is not awarded in which of the following fields?
GK.e: Nobel Prizes are awarded in six fields, but not in mathematics.

GK.q: Which is the national sport of Japan?
GK.e: Sumo wrestling is Japan’s national sport, having originated there centuries ago.

GK.q: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
GK.e: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

GK.q: The Border Security Force (BSF) was established in which year?
GK.e: The BSF was raised in 1965 after the Indo-Pak war to guard India’s borders.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian to win the Magsaysay Award?
GK.e: Vinoba Bhave, a Gandhian social reformer, won the Magsaysay Award in 1958 for his Bhoodan movement.

GK.q: Which Indian city is called the "City of Joy"?
GK.e: Kolkata is called the "City of Joy," a phrase popularized by Dominique Lapierre’s book of the same name.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win the Jnanpith Award?
GK.e: Bengali novelist Ashapurna Devi was the first Indian woman to win the Jnanpith Award in 1976.

GK.q: World Health Day is celebrated on
GK.e: World Health Day is celebrated every year on 7th April, marking the founding of the World Health Organization in 1948.

GK.q: Who was the first Indian to win an Olympic medal?
GK.e: K.D. Jadhav won a bronze medal in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, becoming the first Indian to win an Olympic medal.

GK.q: Which is the largest desert in the world?
GK.e: The Sahara Desert in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9.2 million sq km. Only Antarctica and the Arctic are larger, but they are cold deserts.

GK.q: The longest river in the world is
GK.e: The Nile River in Africa is about 6650 km long, making it the world’s longest river. However, some recent studies suggest the Amazon may be slightly longer depending on measuring sources.

GK.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in
GK.e: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa (5895 m), is located in Tanzania. It is a dormant volcanic mountain with three cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira.

GK.q: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
GK.e: Vatican City, an independent state within Rome (Italy), is the smallest country in the world with an area of only 0.44 sq km.

GK.q: The "Land of the Rising Sun" refers to
GK.e: Japan is known as the "Land of the Rising Sun" because it lies to the east of the Asian continent and is among the first places where the sun rises.

GK.q: Which continent is known as the "Dark Continent"?
GK.e: Africa was historically called the "Dark Continent" by Europeans due to lack of exploration and knowledge about its interior until the 19th century.

GK.q: Which country is called the "Land of a Thousand Lakes"?
GK.e: Finland has over 1,80,000 lakes and is popularly called the "Land of a Thousand Lakes."

GK.q: Which country is separated from Europe by the Ural Mountains?
GK.e: The Ural Mountains act as a natural boundary between Europe and Asia. Russia spans both continents.

GK.q: Which ocean is the largest in the world?
GK.e: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about 46% of Earth’s water surface and 32% of its total surface area.

GK.q: The Dead Sea lies between
GK.e: The Dead Sea is a salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east and Israel to the west. It is one of the saltiest bodies of water and lies about 430 m below sea level.

GK.q: The Great Barrier Reef is located in
GK.e: The Great Barrier Reef, the world’s largest coral reef system, is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

GK.q: Which is the longest mountain range in the world?
GK.e: The Andes in South America is the longest continental mountain range, stretching about 7,000 km through seven countries including Chile, Argentina, Peru, and Colombia.

GK.q: Which country has the highest number of time zones?
GK.e: Due to its overseas territories, France has the highest number of time zones (12). Russia has 11, while the USA has 9.

GK.q: The world’s largest island is
GK.e: Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark, is the world’s largest island with an area of 2.16 million sq km.

GK.q: Which river is known as the "Yellow River"?
GK.e: The Huang He in China is called the "Yellow River" because of the loess sediments that give its waters a yellowish color.

GK.q: The Panama Canal connects
GK.e: The Panama Canal, completed in 1914, connects the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans through the Isthmus of Panama, enabling faster global trade.

GK.q: The Tropic of Cancer does not pass through which of the following countries?
GK.e: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 16 countries including India, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, but not through Egypt.

GK.q: The highest waterfall in the world is
GK.e: Angel Falls in Venezuela has a height of 979 m, making it the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.

GK.q: Which sea is the warmest in the world?
GK.e: The Red Sea has the warmest water in the world, with average temperatures ranging from 21°C to 30°C due to its location in a hot desert region.

GK.q: Which country is known as the "Horn of Africa"?
GK.e: Somalia forms the easternmost projection of Africa into the Arabian Sea, known as the Horn of Africa.

GK.q: The "Ring of Fire" is located in
GK.e: The Pacific "Ring of Fire" is a zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions around the Pacific Ocean, due to tectonic plate movements.

GK.q: Which is the saltiest lake in the world?
GK.e: Don Juan Pond in Antarctica has salinity over 40%, making it the saltiest natural body of water. The Dead Sea is also highly saline but less so.

GK.q: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
GK.e: The Bering Strait separates Russia (Asia) from Alaska (North America) with a width of about 85 km.

GK.q: The largest peninsula in the world is
GK.e: The Arabian Peninsula, covering about 3.2 million sq km, is the largest peninsula in the world, comprising countries like Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, and UAE.

GK.q: Which is the deepest point in the world’s oceans?
GK.e: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean has the Challenger Deep, the deepest point on Earth at about 11,034 meters.

GK.q: Which is the coldest inhabited place on Earth?
GK.e: Oymyakon in Siberia holds the record for the coldest inhabited place on Earth, with temperatures reaching –71°C.

GK.q: Which city is known as the "City of Canals"?
GK.e: Venice (Italy), Amsterdam (Netherlands), and Bangkok (Thailand) are all called "City of Canals" due to their extensive canal networks.

GK.q: The Suez Canal connects
GK.e: The Suez Canal in Egypt connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, providing the shortest sea link between Europe and Asia.

GK.q: The Great Victoria Desert is located in
GK.e: The Great Victoria Desert is the largest desert in Australia, spanning over 424,400 sq km across Western and South Australia.

GK.q: Which plateau is known as the "Roof of the World"?
GK.e: The Tibetan Plateau is called the "Roof of the World" because it is the highest and largest plateau, with an average elevation of over 4,500 meters above sea level.

Hindi.q: कारक के कितने भेद होते हैं?

Hindi.e: अपादान कारक का विभक्ति चिह्न 'से' होता है, जिसका प्रयोग किसी वस्तु या व्यक्ति के अलग होने (अलगाव), डरने या तुलना के भाव में किया जाता है।

Hindi.q: 'वृक्ष से पत्ते गिरते हैं' इस वाक्य में कौन-सा कारक है?

Hindi.q: 'वह बाज खम्बे पर बैठा है' वाक्य में कौन-सा कारक है?

Hindi.q: 'तोता डाली पर बैठा है' इस वाक्य में कौन-सा कारक है?
Hindi.e: 'डाली पर' स्थान का बोध कराता है, इसलिए यह अधिकरण कारक है।

Hindi.q: 'पिता ने पुत्र को डण्डे से मारा' इस वाक्य में कौन-सा कारक है?

Hindi.q: 'मुँह में राम बगल में छुरी' लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है
opts: ईश्वर के नाम पर छल करना

Hindi.q: 'सब धान बाइस पंसेरी' लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है

Hindi.q: 'घाट-घाट का पानी पीना' लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है

Hindi.q: 'काठ की हाण्डी एक बार ही चढ़ती है' लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है
