Reasoning.q: A person walks 4 km North, then 3 km West, and finally 12 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Use Pythagoras to get displacement.

Reasoning.q: Ramesh starts facing North. He turns right, walks 4 m, turns right again, walks 3 m, and then turns left and walks 5 m. In which direction is he now facing?
Reasoning.e: Track turns step by step.

Reasoning.q: A man walks 8 m East, then 6 m North, then 8 m West, and finally 6 m South. Where is he from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Movements cancel each other.

Reasoning.q: A child goes 15 m North, then 10 m East, then 15 m South. How far is he from his starting point?
Reasoning.e: Net displacement calculated via horizontal movement.

Reasoning.q: Anu faces West. She turns left, walks 5 m, turns right, walks 7 m, and finally turns left and walks 10 m. Which direction is she facing?
Reasoning.e: Left and right turns change facing accordingly.

Reasoning.q: A bus goes 10 km North, 15 km East, 10 km South, and 5 km West. How far is it from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Net East-West and North-South displacements combined.

Reasoning.q: A girl goes 18 m North, then 24 m East. How far is she from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Distance = √(18² + 24²).

Reasoning.q: A person moves 6 km North, 8 km East, 6 km South, and 2 km West. How far is he from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Combine horizontal and vertical displacements.

Reasoning.q: A train goes 10 km West, then 12 km North, then 10 km East. How far is it from the starting point?
Reasoning.e: Net position found using Pythagoras.

Reasoning.q: A man goes 5 km East, 12 km North, and then 5 km West. How far is he from his starting point?
Reasoning.e: Only vertical displacement matters after cancellation.

Reasoning.q: Who amongst Sameer, Milon, Arjun, and Priya is the oldest if Sameer is older than Milon but not as old as Arjun, and Priya is older than Sameer but not as old as Milon?
Reasoning.e: Order → Arjun > Sameer > Milon > Priya. Arjun is the oldest.

Reasoning.q: In a race among five girls, Sonam finished before Neha but after Pooja. Shivani finished before Anju but after Neha. Who won the race?
Reasoning.e: Order → Pooja > Sonam > Neha > Shivani > Anju. Pooja is first.

Reasoning.q: If Anita is taller than Surjit but shorter than Kusum, and Surjit is as tall as Kalpana but taller than Vanita, then what is the relation between Kalpana and Anita?
Reasoning.e: Kusum > Anita > Surjit = Kalpana > Vanita.

Reasoning.q: In a group of five districts, Akbarpur is smaller than Fatehpur, Dhanbad is bigger than Palamu, and Barabanki is bigger than Fatehpur but not as big as Palamu. Which district is the biggest?
Reasoning.e: Order → Dhanbad > Palamu > Barabanki > Fatehpur > Akbarpur.

Reasoning.q: Five friends A, B, C, D, and E are sitting in a row in decreasing order of weight from left to right. A is heavier than only C, B is heavier than both E and A, and D is heavier than B. Who is sitting in the centre?
Reasoning.e: Order → D > B > E > A > C. Middle is E.

Reasoning.q: In a queue of girls, Shama is 11th from the start and 27th from the end. How many girls are in the queue?
In a row of 50 people, Sachin is 24th from the right end. What is his position from the left end?
Reasoning.e: Position = 50 - 24 + 1 = 27.

Reasoning.q: In a list of 48 students, Rohit’s rank is 41st from the bottom. Find his rank from the top.
Reasoning.e: Rank from top = 48 - 41 + 1 = 8.

Reasoning.q: In a row of trees, one tree is 7th from either end. How many trees are there in the row?
If you are 9th in a queue from one end and 11th from the other end, what is the total number of persons in the queue?
Rajesh’s rank is 12th from top and 30th from bottom in the list of passed students. If 16 children failed, how many appeared for the exam?
In an examination, Rahul got 11th rank from top and 47th from bottom among those who passed. 3 students did not appear and 1 failed. What is the total number of students?
In a queue of 17 people, when Seema moves 3 positions left, she becomes 6th from left. What was her previous position from the right?
Reasoning.e: Original position from left = 6 + 3 = 9. From right = 17 - 9 + 1 = 9.

Reasoning.q: Umesh is taller than Satish. Suresh is shorter than Neeraj but taller than Umesh. Who is the tallest?
Reasoning.e: Order → Neeraj > Suresh > Umesh > Satish.

Reasoning.q: P, Q, R, and S are four friends. P is shorter than Q but taller than R, who is shorter than S. Who is the shortest?
Reasoning.e: Order → S > Q > P > R. R is the shortest.

Reasoning.q: In a line of 40 students, Neha is 12th from the left. What is her position from the right?
Reasoning.e: Total – Left + 1 gives position from right.

Reasoning.q: In a class of 60 students, Ramesh is ranked 25th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
Reasoning.e: Total – Top + 1 gives rank from bottom.

Reasoning.q: In a row of 25 people, A is 10th from the left and B is 18th from the right. How many people are sitting between them?
Reasoning.e: Use formula: (Total – (Left + Right – 1)) for distance.

Reasoning.q: In a queue, Meena is 18th from the front and 15th from the back. How many students are there in the queue?
Reasoning.e: Front + Back – 1 gives total number.

Reasoning.q: In a school exam, Sita ranked 7th from the top and 38th from the bottom. How many students appeared in the exam?
Reasoning.e: Top + Bottom – 1 gives total strength.

Reasoning.q: Four friends A, B, C, and D are standing in a row. A is taller than B but shorter than D. C is shorter than B but taller than A. Who is the shortest?
Reasoning.e: Compare relative positions given.

Reasoning.q: In a race of 20 students, Rohit finished 8th from the top. What is his position from the bottom?
Reasoning.e: Use bottom = Total – Top + 1.

Reasoning.q: In a row of 18 persons, the position of Ritu from the left is 9th. What is her position from the right?
Reasoning.e: Subtract left position from total + 1.

Reasoning.q: In a class of 50 students, Anil’s rank is 14th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
Reasoning.e: Same formula, adjust to bottom rank.

Reasoning.q: A’s rank is 15th from top in a class of 40 students. B is 7 ranks below A. What is B’s rank from bottom?
Reasoning.e: Add ranks difference then convert to bottom.

Reasoning.q: In a queue, Rani is 14th from the front and 19th from the back. How many people are there in the queue?
Reasoning.e: Front + Back – 1.

Reasoning.q: Five persons P, Q, R, S, and T are standing in a line. P is ahead of R but behind Q. S is behind R but ahead of T. Who is standing in the middle?
Reasoning.e: Arrange step by step in order.

Reasoning.q: In a class of 75 students, Kiran is ranked 15th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
Reasoning.e: Bottom = Total – Top + 1.

Reasoning.q: In a row, Seema is 19th from the left end and 12th from the right end. How many people are there in the row?
Reasoning.e: Left + Right – 1 = Total.

Reasoning.q: Six students are standing in a row. A is to the left of B but to the right of C. D is to the left of C but to the right of E. F is to the right of B. Who is in the middle?
Reasoning.e: After arranging all six, A occupies the middle position.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some books are tables. Some tables are mirrors. Conclusions: I. Some mirrors are books. II. Some tables are books.
Reasoning.e: Some books are tables → So, "Some tables are books" is always true. Nothing connects mirrors and books → I does not follow.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All flowers are trees. No fruit is tree. Conclusions: I. No fruit is flower. II. Some trees are flowers.
Reasoning.e: All flowers are trees + No fruit is tree → No fruit is flower. Also, “Some trees are flowers” is true because flowers are part of trees.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some hens are cows. All cows are horses. Conclusions: I. Some horses are hens. II. Some hens are horses.
Reasoning.e: Some hens are cows + All cows are horses → Those cows are horses. So, “Some horses are hens” and “Some hens are horses” both follow.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some pins are clips. Some clips are pens. Conclusions: I. Some pins are pens. II. Some pens are clips.
Reasoning.e: Some clips are pens → So, “Some pens are clips” is valid. No relation proves pins and pens → I does not follow.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some horses are lions. All lions are foxes. Conclusions: I. No fox is horse. II. Some foxes are lions.
Reasoning.e: All lions are foxes → Therefore, “Some foxes are lions.” But nothing shows “No fox is horse.”

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All wheels are brakes. Some gears are wheels. Conclusions: I. No brake is gear. II. Some gears are brakes.
Reasoning.e: Some gears are wheels + All wheels are brakes → Those gears are also brakes. “No brake is gear” cannot be derived.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All men are dogs. All dogs are cats. Conclusions: I. All men are cats. II. All cats are men.
Reasoning.e: All men are dogs + All dogs are cats → All men are cats. But it does not mean all cats are men.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by three conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All pens are roads. All roads are houses. Conclusions: I. All houses are pens. II. Some houses are pens. III. All pens are houses.
Reasoning.e: All pens are roads + All roads are houses → So, all pens are houses. From this, “Some houses are pens” also follows. But “All houses are pens” is not valid.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by three conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All pens are chalks. All chairs are chalks. Conclusions: I. Some pens are chairs. II. Some chalks are pens. III. Some chalks are chairs.
Reasoning.e: All pens are chalks, all chairs are chalks. So, “Some chalks are pens” and “Some chalks are chairs” are true. But there is no relation between pens and chairs.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by three conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All trucks are buses. Some scooters are buses. Conclusions: I. All trucks are scooters. II. No bus is scooter. III. No scooter is bus.
Reasoning.e: All trucks are buses + Some scooters are buses. Nothing says trucks are scooters, or that scooters cannot be buses. So, no conclusion follows.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: Good health is dependent on right eating habits. Most people do not follow any rule regarding eating. Conclusions: I. Most people have poor health. II. People are ignorant of proper eating habits.
Reasoning.e: If health depends on right eating and most people don’t follow rules, then most people have poor health. But ignorance is not directly stated.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: Black cloud follows thunder. Rains follow thunder. Conclusions: I. Thunder is the cause of rain. II. Black cloud is the cause of thunder.
Reasoning.e: “Black cloud follows thunder” and “Rains follow thunder” → This only indicates black cloud is linked to thunder, not that thunder causes rain.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: Workers feel motivated when they participate in management. Conclusions: I. Workers should be motivated to produce more. II. Workers should be allowed to participate in management.
Reasoning.e: Statement says workers feel motivated by participation. So, both “Workers should be motivated to produce more” and “Workers should participate” follow.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: Industrial revolution started in Europe and brought modern age. Conclusions: I. Disparity between rich and poor results in revolution. II. Revolution overhauls society.
Reasoning.e: Statement tells revolution changed society. So, “Revolution overhauls society” follows. But disparity between rich and poor is not mentioned.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: America’s defence secretary reiterated supplying arms to Pakistan. Conclusions: I. Pakistan is incapable of manufacturing arms. II. It would ensure peace in the region.
Reasoning.e: Statement only mentions USA supplying arms. Nothing indicates Pakistan can’t manufacture or that it ensures peace.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two assumptions. Decide which assumption is implicit. Statement: Apart from entertainment, television has educational value. Assumptions: I. People take TV only as entertainment. II. The educational value of TV is not realised properly.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Reasoning.e: Saying TV has educational value assumes people see it only as entertainment (I) and don’t realise its educational side (II). Both implicit.

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two assumptions. Decide which assumption is implicit. Statement: Ten wait-listed candidates could finally be admitted. Assumptions: I. Wait-listed candidates get admission with difficulty. II. A large number of candidates were on the waiting list.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Reasoning.e: Getting admission from waiting list indicates difficulty (I). But number of candidates on the list is not mentioned (II).

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two assumptions. Decide which assumption is implicit. Statement: In Mumbai, railway trains are indispensable for suburban workers. Assumptions: I. Trains are the only mode of transport in suburbs. II. Only trains run punctually.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Reasoning.e: Trains are important for suburbs. But statement does not claim they are the only transport (I) or only punctual (II).

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two assumptions. Decide which assumption is implicit. Statement: The mangoes are too cheap to be good. Assumptions: I. When crop is abundant, prices go down. II. Lower price means inferior quality.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Reasoning.e: “Too cheap to be good” assumes that lower price means poor quality (II). It doesn’t say crop size affects price (I).

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two assumptions. Decide which assumption is implicit. Statement: Of all Delhi newspapers, ‘The Time and Space’ has the largest readers. Assumptions: I. Volume of readership of all newspapers is known. II. No other paper has larger readership.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Reasoning.e: To say one paper has most readers, total readership must be known (I). But it doesn’t deny another paper may be close (II).

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All children are students. All students are players. Conclusions: I. All cricketers are students. II. All children are players.
Reasoning.e: All children are students + All students are players → All children are players (II). Nothing about cricketers (I).

Reasoning.q: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows. Statement: Government announced concessions and packages for foreign tourists. Conclusions: I. More foreign tourists will visit India. II. Government is serious about attracting tourists.
Reasoning.e: Government gave concessions to attract tourists → It assumes this will bring more tourists (I). Seriousness (II) is not logically guaranteed.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All animals are dogs. All dogs are birds. Conclusions: I. All animals are birds. II. All birds are animals.
Reasoning.e: All animals are dogs + All dogs are birds → So, all animals are birds (I). But nothing shows all birds are animals (II).

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All fruits are tasty. Some tasty things are sour. Conclusions: I. Some fruits are sour. II. All tasty things are fruits.
Reasoning.e: Nothing directly links fruits with sour things → I does not follow. “All tasty things are fruits” also not true.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some chairs are tables. All tables are furniture. Conclusions: I. Some chairs are furniture. II. All furniture are tables.
Reasoning.e: Some chairs are tables → those tables are furniture → So, some chairs are furniture. Nothing proves all furniture are tables.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All apples are red. No red is green. Conclusions: I. No apple is green. II. Some greens are not apples.
Reasoning.e: All apples are red and no red is green → So, apples cannot be green. But nothing proves relation of greens with apples for II.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All pens are books. Some books are copies. Conclusions: I. Some pens are copies. II. Some copies are books.
Reasoning.e: All pens are books but no link with copies → I does not follow. “Some copies are books” directly follows from second statement.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: All birds are animals. Some animals are lions. Conclusions: I. Some birds are lions. II. Some animals are birds.
Reasoning.e: Birds are animals but nothing links birds with lions. So only “Some animals are birds” follows.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: Some boys are tall. All tall are strong. Conclusions: I. Some boys are strong. II. All strong are tall.
Reasoning.e: Some boys are tall → those tall boys are strong → So some boys are strong. But strong need not all be tall.

Reasoning.q: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Decide which of the conclusions follow. Statements: No doctor is lazy. Some teachers are lazy. Conclusions: I. No teacher is doctor. II. Some lazy are not doctors.
Reasoning.e: Doctors and teachers relation is not given, so I does not follow. From “No doctor is lazy,” all lazy persons are outside doctors → II follows.

Reasoning.e: baaaba Filling the 6 blanks with “baaaab” gives “abbaabbaabbaab”, i.e., (abba)(abba)(abba)+ab.

Reasoning.q: Choose the option that best completes the series/pattern. m_nnm_n_mmn_m_nn
Reasoning.e: Insert “mmnnm” into the blanks to form a balanced alternation of m- and n-blocks with repeating mm/nn/m structure.

Reasoning.q: Choose the option that best completes the series/pattern. _aab_caa_bbc_a_b_ca
Reasoning.e: Filling with “abaaab” yields “aabcaabbcabcaa”, forming a consistent repetition of “aabca” / “abbca” motifs.

Reasoning.q: Choose the option that best completes the series/pattern. 98_6_87_9_76
Reasoning.e: Insert 7,9,6,8 to get “987698769876”, i.e., the block “9876” repeated thrice.

Reasoning.q: Choose the option that best completes the series/pattern. ZOZZZZ, ZZZZOZ, ZZOZZZ, ZZZOZZ, ?
Reasoning.e: A single ‘O’ shifts position each term (2,5,3,4,6…); next is position 6 → “ZZZZZO”.
